summary: Salesforce has set an ambitious revenue goal of $60 billion by 2034, following its recent achievement of a $10 billion revenue target. This plan involves reaching $20 billion by 2022 and $40 billion by 2028, requiring aggressive acquisitions and sustained growth to maintain market leadership. The company emphasizes continuous innovation and strategic purchases to stay competitive in the evolving tech landscape.

title: G-III Apparel Group, Applied Optoelectronics, Advanced Micro Devices, Intel and Microsoft highlighted as Zacks Bull and Bear of the Day
summary: Zacks Equity Research identifies G-III Apparel Group as the Bull of the Day due to strong retail brands and expected double-digit earnings growth, while Applied Optoelectronics is named Bear of the Day due to uncertainty in its data center business and declining 2018 estimates. The article also discusses Advanced Micro Devices' stock surge after announcing its processors are unaffected by a major security bug impacting Intel CPUs.

title: Northrop Grumman layoffs target 82 South Bay employees
summary: Northrop Grumman is eliminating 82 positions at its El Segundo and Redondo Beach facilities in the South Bay, with additional layoffs of 51 employees in San Diego. The company states these layoffs are a resource alignment with customer needs, amidst significant growth and ongoing efforts to match employee skills with open positions across the company. Northrop Grumman continues its operations including building crucial parts for the U.S. Navy’s F/A-18 Super Hornet, an $80 billion deal for the B-21 Raider bomber, and constructing the $8.7 billion James Webb Space Telescope.

title: Leverage Shares 2X Long CRWV Daily ETF (CRWG) interactive stock chart
summary: This page from Yahoo Finance displays an interactive stock chart for the Leverage Shares 2X Long CRWV Daily ETF (CRWG). It provides current pricing, after-hours figures, and links to news, historical data, and related tickers. The page also includes general market indices and trending stock information.

title: Brookfield Business Partners to buy Westinghouse for $4.6 billion
summary: Brookfield Business Partners plans to acquire Westinghouse Electric Co LLC, the bankrupt nuclear services company owned by Toshiba Corp, for $4.6 billion. This deal marks Brookfield's first investment in nuclear power and is expected to close in the third quarter of 2018, pending regulatory approval. Westinghouse, a leading supplier in the nuclear industry, accumulated significant debt from fixed-price contracts for new plant constructions, leading to its bankruptcy filing in March.

title: Western Union settles New York money laundering probe for $60 million
summary: Western Union Co. will pay $60 million to New York's financial regulator to resolve allegations that it failed for over a decade to maintain an adequate anti-money laundering program. This settlement follows a 2017 agreement to pay $586 million to the U.S. Department of Justice and Federal Trade Commission for similar claims. The company is required to submit a written plan and progress reports to the New York Department of Financial Services to ensure compliance.

title: A Booming Global Economy Bolsters Commodity ETFs
summary: The global economy's ongoing growth and improved manufacturing activity are driving increased demand for raw materials, benefiting commodity markets and related ETFs. Major broad commodity ETFs like PowerShares DB Commodity Index Tracking Fund (DBC) and iShares S&P GSCI Commodity-Indexed Trust (GSG) have seen significant gains. Experts predict continued global economic expansion in 2018, which is expected to further boost commodity demand and potentially lead to inflationary pressures.

title: Stantec & ENGCOMP to lead PFS for Wheeler River uranium project
summary: Denison Mines Corp has hired Stantec Consulting Inc and ENGCOMP Engineering and Computing Professionals Inc to lead the Pre-Feasibility Study (PFS) for the Wheeler River project, the largest known undeveloped high-grade uranium project in northern Saskatchewan. The PFS aims to determine the best economic options for developing the Gryphon and Phoenix deposits into a large-scale, low-cost uranium mining operation, while also prioritizing sustainability and community benefits. The project is a joint venture between Denison (60%), Cameco Corp (30%), and JCU (Canada) Exploration Co Ltd (10%).

title: Emerging-Market Pioneer Mark Mobius to Retire
summary: Mark Mobius, a prominent emerging-markets guru and executive chairman of Templeton Emerging Markets Group, will retire from Franklin Templeton Investments at the end of the month. He dedicated over three decades to the firm, launching one of the first emerging-market funds in 1987. Mobius gained fame through his investment strategies in Asia, Latin America, Africa, and other frontier markets.

title: Exact Sciences stock is biggest gainer among Wisconsin firms in 2017
summary: Exact Sciences Corp., a Madison-based biotechnology firm, was the top-performing Wisconsin public company in 2017, with its stock price nearly quadrupling despite the company not yet being profitable. The company's Cologuard test for colorectal cancer has driven significant revenue growth, and it is expanding its facilities to meet demand. While one analyst downgraded the stock due to its sharp rally, confidence in the business remains high.

title: Lamb Weston sales, income jump amid strong potato demand
summary: Lamb Weston reported a 4% increase in net sales to $824.6 million and an 11% rise in income during its second quarter, driven by strong potato demand. The company anticipates continued growth, investing in production capacity expansions, and is seen as a potential acquisition target within the growing global potato processing market.

title: The green bond evolution
summary: The green bond market experienced significant growth in 2017, with a 73% year-to-date increase in market value, driven by investor interest in impact investing. While most green bonds fund climate change mitigation projects, the market faces challenges in defining "green" and ensuring transparency, as evidenced by MSCI's rigorous review process. Despite some issuers having lower ESG ratings, the market is evolving, providing opportunities for growth as standards improve and new issuance areas emerge.

title: Emerging Markets Specialist Mark Mobius Retires From Franklin Templeton
summary: Mark Mobius, a renowned investor and one of the earliest to specialize in emerging markets, announced his retirement from Franklin Templeton Investments after more than 30 years. Mobius was instrumental in building the firm's emerging markets group and launched one of the first mutual funds dedicated to these markets. His retirement on January 31, 2018, is not expected to disrupt client services, as a capable team is in place, and Mobius plans to remain active in retirement.

title: Sector ETFs: The State Of Correlations
summary: Correlations among US sector ETFs in 2017 reached new lows, with only one pair exhibiting a correlation above 0.7. The Utilities sector consistently maintained its status as the least correlated with other sectors, offering diversification opportunities. However, investors are cautioned about potential rising correlations during market corrections.

title: Cboe Global Markets reports annual trading volume, several records set in 2017
summary: Cboe Global Markets reported its December and full-year 2017 trading statistics, highlighting several new annual records in index options, S&P 500 options, and Cboe Volatility Index options and futures. The company also noted the debut of Bitcoin Futures on CFE, which saw significant volume in December. Additionally, Cboe provided guidance for its fourth-quarter 2017 average revenue per contract.

title: Greater Washington's newest billionaire is a familiar face — and he won't be distracted
summary: Matt Calkins, CEO of Appian, has become Greater Washington's newest billionaire after his company's stock climbed significantly since its May IPO. Despite this personal milestone, Calkins states he will remain focused on his business. The article highlights his company's successful entry into the public market and its continued growth.

title: Auto dealer complaints, unusual investment seeds USAA’s $330 million venture capital fund
summary: USAA's venture capital fund grew out of original customer complaints about auto dealers, leading to an operational contract and later an investment in TrueCar. This success prompted USAA to establish a Corporate Development division in 2009, overseeing a $330 million fund that invests in companies benefiting its members. The fund focuses on fintech, insurtech, security/AI, and enterprise infrastructure, having invested in over 25 companies including ID.me, Snapsheet, RepairPal, and Coinbase.

title: DTEC Stock Fund Price and Chart — AMEX:DTEC
summary: This article provides a detailed overview of the ALPS Disruptive Technologies ETF (DTEC), traded on the NYSE American. It covers key financial statistics such as assets under management, dividend yield, and expense ratio, along with an in-depth description of its investment strategy, which focuses on 10 disruptive technology themes. The article also includes performance charts, holdings breakdown, and frequently asked questions about the ETF.

title: Trial Over Theft of Wind Technology Spotlights U.S.-China Tensions
summary: A trial is set to begin in Wisconsin concerning the alleged theft of wind-turbine technology by Chinese company Sinovel Wind Group Co. Ltd. from American Superconductor Corp. This case highlights ongoing intellectual-property disputes between the U.S. and China. The loss of Sinovel's business previously caused a significant plunge in AMSC's stock and led to hundreds of layoffs.

title: Southwest Airlines Settles Suit but Denies Colluding to Keep Ticket Prices High (Published 2018)
summary: Southwest Airlines has agreed to a $15 million settlement in a class-action lawsuit alleging collusion with competitors to keep ticket prices high and limit seat availability. While settling to avoid litigation costs, Southwest denies any wrongdoing or unlawful agreements. The airline will also provide "extensive cooperation" and information to the plaintiffs, a move that distinguishes it from American Airlines, Delta Air Lines, and United Airlines, who continue to fight the allegations.

title: U.S. fund managers expect value stocks to jump in 2018
summary: U.S. fund managers are shifting their focus to value stocks in early 2018, anticipating a jump in overlooked shares after a strong year for growth stocks in 2017. Despite past trends where growth stocks continued to lead after strong market years, some managers are actively underweighting technology and increasing positions in financials, industrial companies, and retailers with attractive valuations. They see these value-oriented investments as having significant upside potential over the next couple of years.

title: iShares Core MSCI Emerging Markets ETF ETF Price, Holdings, & News (NYSEARCA:IEMG)
summary: The iShares Core MSCI Emerging Markets ETF (IEMG) tracks the MSCI Emerging Markets IMI index, offering exposure to emerging market firms. As of March 26, 2026, IEMG trades at $68.16, showing a 1.4% increase year-to-date, with major holdings including Taiwan Semiconductor and Samsung Electronics. The ETF has $137.64 billion in assets under management and a net expense ratio of 0.09%.

title: Fixed Income Securities
summary: This article from CommSec details Fixed Income Securities, including an overview of what they are, how they work, and their benefits and risks. It covers various types like Australian Government Bonds, Corporate Bonds, Hybrid Securities, Exchange Traded Bonds (XTBs), and Exchange Traded Funds (ETFs), along with brokerage rates and management expenses. The article aims to inform investors about incorporating fixed income into their portfolios for regular income and diversification.

title: Bright spot for Trump in 2017, job creation faces new challenges
summary: President Donald Trump's first year in office, 2017, saw significant job creation and a falling unemployment rate, marking a key success despite the overall annual job creation being the lowest since 2010. While specific industries like manufacturing and coal mining also added jobs, challenges remain regarding the labor force participation rate and stagnant wages. The article suggests that while the numbers are good, they are not exceptional and largely align with existing trends, with the full impact of policies like the tax cut still to be seen.

title: Viracon plant to close, eliminating 200 jobs in St. George
summary: Viracon announced the permanent closure of its St. George glass manufacturing plant in March 2018, resulting in the elimination of nearly 200 jobs. The closure is attributed to increased automation at its parent company, Apogee Enterprises Inc., and not the St. George plant's performance. St. George city officials and the Department of Workforce Services are working to assist the affected employees in finding new employment within the growing local economy.

title: South Dakota tribes sue drugmakers over opioid painkillers
summary: Three Native American tribes in South Dakota have filed a lawsuit against several opioid industry players, including Purdue Pharma and McKesson Corp., alleging deceptive marketing practices. The lawsuit highlights the disproportionate impact of the opioid crisis on Native American populations, citing higher rates of opioid use for non-medical reasons and overdose deaths. This case is one of many similar lawsuits nationwide but uniquely ties the allegations to the specific harm experienced by tribal communities.

title: CIBC dives back into tech sector with Wellington Financial acquisition
summary: CIBC is re-entering Canada's technology sector through the acquisition of Wellington Financial, a private specialty finance firm, for an undisclosed sum. This deal establishes a new business line, CIBC Innovation Banking, led by Mark McQueen, and aims to provide comprehensive financial services to early- and mid-stage tech companies across North America. The move signifies CIBC's renewed focus on the flourishing Canadian tech industry and positions it to compete more effectively with U.S. lenders.

title: Equifax: Credit Reports & Scores Guide
summary: This guide provides an overview of Equifax, one of the three major credit reporting agencies, detailing its company profile, services, and how it handles consumer credit information. It explains who can access Equifax credit reports, discusses security measures including past data breaches, and outlines how Equifax scores are generated and how consumers can improve their scores. The article also provides a guide on how to read an Equifax credit report.

title: Waste Not, Want Not
summary: This article by Hormel Foods discusses the significant issue of food waste, highlighting its environmental, social, and economic impacts globally and in the United States. It explores solutions such as portion control (single-serve sizes), extending product shelf life, and corporate donations to hunger relief efforts. The piece also details how Hormel Foods and other companies are collaborating to reduce food waste across the industry.

title: Peter Chapman
summary: This article features Peter Chapman, President and CEO of IonQ, highlighting his recommended summer reading. He suggests "The Ride of a Lifetime" by Bob Iger and "That Will Never Work" by Marc Randolph, offering insights into leadership, entrepreneurship, and overcoming challenges. The article also lists other prominent business, global, technology, and media leaders along with their recommended books.

title: Southwest Airlines Agrees to $15M Ticket Price-Fixing Settlement
summary: Southwest Airlines has reached a $15 million settlement in a class action lawsuit alleging it conspired with other airlines to fix ticket prices. The settlement requires Southwest to pay into a fund and cooperate with ongoing litigation against Delta, United, and American Airlines. The case involves allegations that airlines restricted domestic flight capacity to increase airfares, impacting consumers who purchased flights within the U.S. between July 1, 2011, and December 20, 2017.

title: Mohawk to expand in Rockbridge County creating 15 jobs
summary: Mohawk Industries Inc. plans to invest $10 million to expand its manufacturing operation in Glasgow, Rockbridge County, creating 15 new jobs. The Georgia-based company is a global manufacturer of various residential and commercial flooring products. The expansion was announced by Gov. Terry McAuliffe.

title: Traffic updates at Carillon bring 650 new jobs to Raymond James (Video)
summary: Raymond James' decision to expand operations, bringing 650 new jobs, was significantly influenced by St. Petersburg's and FDOT's commitment to address traffic congestion in the Gateway area. This expansion highlights the importance of infrastructure improvements in corporate location decisions.

title: Consumer Discretionary ETFs Head to Head: XLY vs. VCR
summary: This article compares two consumer discretionary ETFs, XLY and VCR, highlighting their exposure, holdings, and performance. Fueled by strong consumer demand and positive economic trends, the consumer discretionary sector is attracting significant investor attention. While XLY has higher AUM, VCR offers a cheaper expense ratio and greater diversification, with both showing similar performance.

title: Why GoPro CEO Nick Woodman Cannot Be Fired
summary: GoPro CEO Nicholas Woodman cannot be fired despite the company's struggles because he controls 99.08% of Class B stock, representing 76.81% of the total voting power. This concentrated control, detailed in the company's 10-K, allows Woodman to dictate all matters, including board elections and major corporate transactions, leaving unhappy investors with no options. The company recently cut its fourth-quarter estimate and announced layoffs, exiting the drone business, which sent shares falling.

title: 13D Filing: Delta Partners and Good Times Restaurants Inc. (GTIM)
summary: This 13D filing details activities and intentions of Delta Partners regarding Good Times Restaurants Inc. (GTIM). It outlines the source of shares received by Delta Partners and the Jobson Family Foundation, as well as communications with GTIM's board concerning stockholder lists, concerns about recent actions, and proposals for maximizing shareholder value, including refranchising and expansion strategies.

title: LTL freight demand surges, tough negotiations underway at ABF Freight
summary: Demand for less-than-truckload (LTL) carriers is rising, leading to accelerated pricing trends. However, ArcBest's subsidiary, ABF Freight, faces difficult negotiations with the Teamsters union as its contract expires in March 2018. Analysts have downgraded ArcBest shares due to concerns over ABF Freight's competitive disadvantage with union labor and potential concessions in the upcoming negotiations, despite overall positive industry trends.

title: Ablynx soars after rejects Novo Nordisk's $3.1 billion biotech bid
summary: Ablynx rejected a 2.6 billion euro ($3.1 billion) takeover bid from Novo Nordisk, sending its shares up 45 percent. Novo Nordisk, the world's largest insulin maker, is seeking to expand into rare blood disorders, but analysts predict it may need to raise its bid and could face counterbidders. Ablynx considered the offer to fundamentally undervalue the company, though its chairman resigned immediately after the announcement.

title: Number Of Proposed Bitcoin ETFs Grows
summary: The number of proposed Bitcoin ETFs is increasing, with Direxion Funds being the latest to file for leveraged/inverse strategies. Since the initial Winklevoss brothers' proposal, 23 filings for Bitcoin ETFs have reached regulators, largely driven by the reality of bitcoin futures. While regulators have not yet signaled approval, investors can currently access bitcoin through ARK Invest funds (ARKW and ARKK) which hold an approximate 7% allocation to the cryptocurrency.

title: CES 2018: Kodak soars on KodakCoin and Bitcoin mining plans
summary: Eastman Kodak saw its shares soar by nearly 120% after announcing plans for a crypto-currency called KodakCoin and a Bitcoin mining operation, Kodak KashMiner, at CES 2018. KodakCoin is intended to help photographers manage image rights, while KashMiner will allow customers to rent Bitcoin mining capacity at Kodak's headquarters. This move is part of Kodak's post-bankruptcy strategy of licensing its brand and leveraging its existing infrastructure, though some experts question the real value added by blockchain for copyright and warn of a "frothy investment market" around crypto.

title: C&W parent completes Caribbean split-off
summary: Liberty Global has completed the separation of its Latin American and Caribbean businesses, including Flow's Cayman branch, into a new entity called Liberty Latin America. This move aims to reduce Liberty Global's U.S. tax bill and allow the new entity to raise capital independently and attract investment in higher-growth Latin American markets. Liberty Latin America's stock is now trading on the Nasdaq Global Select Market.

title: Bitcoin Futures Trading Isn't Blowing Up — Yet
summary: The article discusses the initial subdued trading volume of Bitcoin futures despite their perceived advantages, such as regulation and hedging opportunities. It highlights that institutional investors need time to adapt and that the high cost of entry and complexity deter individual traders. Despite the slow start, the author suggests that Bitcoin futures could pave the way for more institutional investment vehicles like ETFs.

title: Invention: A Look Back at Historic Firsts With North Texas Ties
summary: This article highlights various historic inventions and firsts that have North Texas origins, ranging from everyday items to significant technological advancements. It showcases the contributions of North Texas inventors and companies to the world.

title: Hudbay Minerals to Buy 3 Properties in Peru
summary: Hudbay Minerals, through its subsidiary Hudbay Peru, has agreed to acquire three mining properties—Caballito, Maria Reyna, and Kusiorcco—in Peru, near its Constancia copper porphyry project. These acquisitions aim to expand Hudbay's copper exploration efforts, particularly as copper prices are expected to remain supported in 2018. The company is beginning the permitting and technical activities required for drilling on these new concessions.

title: Nine Energy Service, Inc. Announces Launch of Initial Public Offering
summary: Nine Energy Service, Inc. announced the launch of its initial public offering of 7,000,000 shares of common stock, with an additional option for underwriters to purchase up to 1,050,000 shares. The expected initial offering price is between $20.00 and $23.00 per share, and the shares will be listed on the New York Stock Exchange under the ticker symbol “NINE.” J.P. Morgan, Goldman Sachs & Co. LLC, and Wells Fargo Securities are acting as joint book-running managers for the offering.

title: Prologis Completes 13 Build-to-Suit Development Projects in the Second Half of 2017 Totaling more than 4.7 Million Square Feet
summary: Prologis, Inc. announced the completion of 13 build-to-suit development projects in the second half of 2017, totaling over 4.7 million square feet with an expected investment of approximately $350 million. For the full year 2017, the company completed 33 build-to-suit projects encompassing more than 12 million square feet and started 38 build-to-suits with a total expected investment of about $1.1 billion. This robust activity, driven by a strong land bank and multi-site customers focused on e-commerce, marks the highest level of build-to-suit activity relative to overall development starts since 2013.

title: FedEx Express Opens Mammoth Shanghai Hub, Touts Improved Asia Linkage
summary: FedEx Express has officially opened a new 1.4 million square foot Shanghai hub at Shanghai Pudong International Airport, representing an investment of over $100 million. This facility significantly expands FedEx's presence in one of the world's fastest-growing markets, more than tripling its previous footprint in Shanghai. The new hub features cutting-edge technology, including a fully automated sorting system with a capacity of up to 36,000 packages per hour, and cold chain facilities for temperature-sensitive items, aiming to enhance operational efficiency and improve access to international markets for Asia Pacific customers.

title: Charting a bull-trend breakout, S&P 500 reaches ‘clear skies’ territory
summary: The S&P 500 has achieved a bull-trend breakout, entering "clear skies" territory according to MarketWatch's Technical Indicator. This indicates a strong start to 2018 for major U.S. benchmarks, which have reached uncharted highs. The article also notes the 10-year yield extending its breakout and Europe's market tagging a three-year peak.

title: Trucking Industry Struggles With Growing Driver Shortage
summary: The U.S. trucking industry is facing a significant driver shortage, with the American Trucking Associations stating a need for almost 900,000 more drivers. This shortage is delaying nonessential shipments and increasing delivery costs, fueled by an aging workforce, the demanding lifestyle of truckers, and difficulties attracting new entrants to the profession despite recent wage increases.

title: Native American tribes sue opioid manufacturers, distributors
summary: Three Native American tribes in the Dakotas have sued 24 opioid industry groups, including manufacturers like Purdue Pharma and distributors like McKesson Corp., alleging they concealed and minimized the addiction risk of prescription drugs. This lawsuit is among the first to directly link claims to the drugs' impact on Native Americans, who experienced a disproportionately high rate of prescription opioid misuse and opioid-related deaths. The tribes seek monetary damages and an "abatement fund" to support treatment programs, highlighting the overwhelming burden on their public health and law enforcement services due to the opioid crisis.

title: Huawei's AT&T U.S. smartphone deal collapses
summary: Huawei's planned deal with AT&T to sell its smartphones in the U.S. collapsed due to security concerns raised by U.S. lawmakers. This setback significantly impacts the Chinese firm's ambitions in the U.S. market, where it holds a very small share. Despite the challenge, Huawei stated its commitment to the U.S. market, focusing on open channel sales for its Mate 10 Pro.

title: Golar LNG seen as worthy over long-term
summary: Evercore ISI has named Golar LNG as a "top long idea" for the third consecutive year, suggesting its long-term value. Golar LNG's general partner, Golar LNG Partners, is also highlighted, specifically mentioning their Hilli Episeyo floating liquefied natural gas platform. The article emphasizes Golar LNG's potential for sustained growth and positive performance.

title: Bitcoin Powers Big Returns for a Pair of ETFs
summary: Two ETFs managed by Ark Investment Management have shown significant returns, over 97% since the end of 2016, largely due to their holdings in Bitcoin. These funds demonstrate that some investment firms are incorporating cryptocurrencies without waiting for specific U.S. regulatory approvals for Bitcoin-exclusive ETFs. Despite the rising mainstream acceptance of Bitcoin, the risk of hacks and scandals has also increased.

title: The global LiDAR market is booming
summary: The global LiDAR market is projected to reach USD 5,842.37 million by 2024, growing at a CAGR of 24.1% from 2017 to 2024, driven by increased demand for drones and technological advancements. Key players include Teledyne Optech, Hexagon, Sick AG, and Trimble Inc., with the market being highly concentrated. The report highlights market drivers, restraints, competitive landscape, and segmented forecasts across various applications and geographies.

title: Lockheed Martin seeking 100 jobs at Owego site
summary: Lockheed Martin is seeking to fill 100 open technical positions at its Owego site, part of a total of 200 openings across its Syracuse and Owego locations. These positions are a result of retirements and programs transitioning from development to production, spanning various engineering fields and technician roles. The company is hosting a job fair at Destiny USA mall in Syracuse to answer questions about these competitive-salary positions.

title: Countdown to Human-Free Construction in Less Than 10 Years
summary: This article forecasts a future of highly automated construction, predicting human-free job sites within a decade due to accelerating sensor and software technology. It outlines a timeline from 2018 to 2025, detailing the integration of SaaS, IoT, AR, pre-fab construction, 3D printing, drones, and AI. The author also discusses the impending labor displacement and the need for immediate conversations about automation's societal impact.

title: TeleTech Announces Name Change to TTEC
summary: TeleTech Holdings, Inc. has officially changed its name to TTEC (pronounced T-tec) to reflect its evolution into an end-to-end strategic business partner for customer experience. This rebranding follows eight years of innovation and investment in a holistic, technology-enabled customer engagement platform. The company will streamline its go-to-market strategy with "TTEC Digital" focusing on strategic consulting and cloud-based technology, and "TTEC Engage" providing operational excellence in customer acquisition, care, and growth.

title: Building Management System (BMS) Market Growth by Top Key
summary: This article provides an analysis of the global Building Management System (BMS) market, forecasting its growth from 2017 to 2024. Key market drivers include increased demand for energy-efficient systems and growing automation in security, with the market expected to reach USD 54.0 billion by 2016. The report segments the market by software, services, and application, and identifies major competitors and geographical trends.

title: Chicago Rockford International Airport to host job fair
summary: The Chicago Rockford International Airport is hosting a job fair on Tuesday, January 16, from 3 to 7 p.m. in the Main Terminal Building. Numerous companies, including AAR Corp., OSF HealthCare, and UPS, will be present to recruit for various positions. Attendees are encouraged to bring a photo ID and a resume.

title: Computer Vision Company Announces Collaboration with Nvidia, Stock Rallies
summary: Foresight Autonomous Holdings Ltd. (Nasdaq-listed) announced that its affiliate, Rail Vision Ltd., is collaborating with Nvidia Corporation on system development, causing Foresight's stock to jump 18%. Foresight also increased its stake in Rail Vision to 32.62% and announced new pilot agreements with Chinese car manufacturers, while Nvidia expands its presence in the autonomous vehicle market, competing with Mobileye. Rail Vision, which develops an automated early warning system for locomotives, is pursuing European licensing and completed significant investment rounds in 2017.

title: Align Technology’s Growth Prospects amid Increasing Competition
summary: Align Technology is experiencing rapid growth, largely driven by the Chinese market and increasing demand for its Invisalign clear aligners in the teen segment. However, the company is facing growing competition from startups like Candid and Smile Direct Club, which offer direct-to-consumer clear aligner solutions. Align Technology also holds an equity stake in Smile Direct Club and supplies to them, while 3M remains its largest competitor.

title: Bitcoin and blockchain| Gulf Times
summary: This article discusses the rise of Bitcoin and its underlying blockchain technology, highlighting their potential to reshape global financial systems despite skepticism from some financial leaders. It covers Bitcoin's price surge in 2017, the emergence of futures trading, and the broader applications of blockchain beyond cryptocurrencies, such as in equity transactions and supply chain management. The article also touches upon the ongoing debate about Bitcoin's intrinsic value and blockchain's role as a new type of database.

title: A look at Liberty Utilities proposed underground gas pipeline
summary: Liberty Utilities is proposing an underground natural gas pipeline, Granite Bridge, which would run 27 miles from Stratham to Manchester, NH, connecting with existing pipelines and including a new LNG storage tank in Epping. The project faces opposition from environmental activists like Echo Action and skepticism from the state's Consumer Advocate regarding its necessity, impact on ratepayers, and environmental claims, requiring a lengthy approval process. Opponents argue that the capacity claims are disputed by studies and that the project is an unnecessary investment in polluting fossil fuels, advocating for clean energy alternatives.

title: Cintas to close central Des Moines location; job losses expected
summary: Cintas is set to close its central Des Moines stockroom over the next four months, impacting approximately 35 employees. This closure is part of the Cincinnati-based uniform company's strategy to optimize its distribution network, following its 2017 merger with G&K Services. Employees will be offered severance pay, continued health care coverage, and job placement assistance, along with opportunities to apply for positions at other local Cintas facilities.

title: Leadership and Membership Announcements for the Federal Reserve Bank of San Francisco’s Salt Lake City Branch Board of Directors - San Francisco Fed
summary: Patricia R. Richards has been reappointed as director and chair of the Federal Reserve Bank of San Francisco’s Salt Lake City branch board for 2018. Additionally, Russell A. (Chip) Childs, president and CEO of SkyWest Inc., was appointed to the board, and Park Price, chairman and CEO Emeritus of the Bank of Idaho, was reappointed as director. These appointments and reappointments are effective January 1, 2018.
source: Federal Reserve Bank of San Francisco

title: Would you live at the Asheville Mall? Redevelopment plan raises questions, intrigue
summary: The Asheville Mall is embarking on a $45 million redevelopment project that includes multifamily housing units, restaurants, retail stores, and a multiplex movie theater. This ambitious plan seeks to transform the mall into a mixed-use "town center" to combat the decline of traditional shopping malls and meet the demand for rental housing in Asheville. Industry experts suggest this shift toward experience-based environments with residential components is crucial for the long-term viability of aging retail properties.

title: SHYL Stock Fund Price and Chart — AMEX:SHYL
summary: This article provides an overview of the SHYL Xtrackers Short Duration High Yield Bond ETF, covering its price, key statistics like AUM and dividend yield, and detailed information about its investment strategy. It also addresses frequently asked questions regarding ETFs, SHYL's performance, and technical analysis. The fund aims to track a short-term bond index with high-yield corporate debt, focusing on US dollar-denominated bonds with remaining maturities between zero and five years.

title: 13D Filing: Saba Capital and Delaware Enhanced Global Dividend & Income Fund (DEX)
summary: Saba Capital, led by Boaz Weinstein, filed an amended 13D related to the Delaware Enhanced Global Dividend & Income Fund (DEX). The filing indicates that Saba Capital Management holds 1,907,485 shares, representing 12.04% of the class. The SEC filing provides detailed ownership summary including sole and shared voting and dispositive power.

title: SkyWest converts former Midwest Airlines hangars into its largest maintenance facility
summary: SkyWest Airlines has established its largest maintenance facility in Milwaukee by renovating former Midwest Airlines hangars at Mitchell International Airport. This development is expected to boost jobs in Milwaukee County. The new facility will service SkyWest's fleet of 423 aircraft, supporting over 2,000 daily flights across North America in partnership with major airlines.

title: Caterpillar Partnering to Develop Downtown Peoria Block
summary: Caterpillar Inc. and OSF HealthCare are partnering to redevelop an iconic Peoria building at 124 SW Adams Street into OSF HealthCare's new Ministry headquarters. Caterpillar is also donating the Peoria Professional Building, an adjacent parking lot, and $3 million to OSF for additional development. This partnership aims to revitalize downtown Peoria, attract and retain talent, and is expected to bring over 700 OSF employees to the downtown area once completed.

title: Israel autorizó el ingreso de carne enfriada desde la Argentina
summary: Israel has authorized the entry of chilled beef from Argentina, a move announced during Vice President Gabriela Michetti's visit. This decision extends the shelf life of Argentine fresh chilled beef from 45 to 85 days, significantly boosting export opportunities for producers, especially for kosher products sold in supermarkets. The announcement is expected to expand the current USD 7 million kosher beef business significantly and strengthen trade relations between the two countries.

title: Cramer shares 5 reasons why the retail sector is back in action, according to industry executives
summary: Jim Cramer identified five key factors contributing to the resurgence of the retail sector, challenging Wall Street's skepticism. These factors include a stronger consumer base, millennials starting families, effective on- and offline strategies from traditional retailers, market share gains by surviving companies, and undervalued stock valuations in some retail giants like Nordstrom and Macy's. Cramer suggests that the sector is now "investable" after years of decline.

title: A.I. Has Arrived in Investing. Humans Are Still Dominating. (Published 2018)
summary: Artificial intelligence is becoming increasingly involved in investment decisions, from high-frequency trading to long-term stock selection, with one ETF even using A.I. algorithms for its holdings. While some believe A.I. will remain a subordinate tool for human fund managers, others envision it taking more control. Experts debate its role and define true A.I. in this context as machine learning that can update itself based on new information, unlike static programs.

title: JPMorgan’s Profits Are Strong, and They’ll Likely Get Stronger (Published 2018)
summary: JPMorgan Chase reported stronger-than-expected Q4 earnings in 2018, despite a $2.4 billion charge related to the new tax law. The bank's results, viewed as a bellwether for the financial industry, indicate that the new lower corporate tax rate will significantly boost future profitability for JPMorgan and its peers, such as Wells Fargo. While its investment bank struggled, JPMorgan's consumer-banking business showed strong growth and is expected to accelerate further with rising interest rates and a strong economy.

title: First Majestic expands Mexico footprint with $320M Primero Mining acquisition
summary: First Majestic Silver has announced the acquisition of Primero Mining in a CAD$320 million cash and stock deal, including debt. This acquisition grants First Majestic access to Primero's flagship San Dimas silver-gold mine in Durango, Mexico. The deal also involves Wheaton Precious Metals replacing its existing silver purchase agreement with Primero with a new contract with First Majestic, linking the stream to both gold and silver production.

title: Power plant controversy peaks in New Orleans
summary: Entergy Corp. is facing significant opposition in New Orleans regarding its proposal to build a new natural gas-fired power plant. Critics advocate for renewable energy solutions, while Entergy argues the plant is necessary for reliability, especially given New Orleans' vulnerability to hurricanes. The decision now rests with a committee of the New Orleans City Council amidst a debate over fossil fuels versus cleaner energy alternatives.

title: What UK Manufacturing Activity Indicates for the Economy
summary: UK manufacturing activity in December 2017 saw a decline in its PMI to 56.3, missing expectations, primarily due to slower production, new orders, and employment growth. Despite this, the broader UK economy had shown strong improvement in the preceding months, with GDP growth and rising inflation leading to an interest rate hike. The article notes that while domestic demand weakened, client orders from Europe, China, and the Middle East rose strongly, and the iShares MSCI United Kingdom ETF (EWU) rose by 2.2% in December 2017.

title: Carrier plant layoffs: Worker thought Trump would save her job. She was wrong.
summary: Renee Elliott, a Carrier plant worker, was one of 215 employees laid off despite believing Donald Trump would save her job following his campaign promise. She expresses deep disappointment, as her hopes were raised by Trump's public statements and a deal to save jobs at the Indianapolis plant. Elliott now faces the daunting prospect of unemployment at 44, concerned about matching her previous $18-an-hour wage and the loss of camaraderie with her co-workers.

title: HP Inc leads PC market amid falling global shipments: Gartner
summary: HP Inc. retained the top spot in the global PC market in Q4 2017 with a 22.5% market share, despite a 2% decline in worldwide PC shipments. The company saw YoY growth across all regions, including the US market, while overall shipments for 2017 fell by 2.8% from 2016, marking the 13th consecutive quarter of decline. Gartner analysts suggest that future PC buyers will prioritize quality and functionality, potentially increasing average selling prices and improving profitability in the long run.

title: MoneyGram Opens Office in Brussels
summary: MoneyGram International Inc. confirmed on Friday that it has opened an office in Brussels and has been granted a license as a payment provider by the National Bank of Belgium. This move was prompted by the uncertainty surrounding Brexit, as MoneyGram sought to ensure its business continuity, despite its European headquarters remaining in London. The company also stated it would continue to be registered with the UK's Financial Conduct Authority and maintain operations in Britain.

title: Equinix to Build More Owned Data Centers with “Nodes” for Cloud Giants
summary: Equinix plans to build more owned data centers with 1MW to 2MW "nodes" specifically for hyper-scale cloud and SaaS providers, including Amazon Web Services, Microsoft Azure, Google Cloud Platform, Facebook, and Apple. This strategy aims to capture the next wave of cloud deployments and secure competitive advantage by attracting profitable enterprise customers, despite lower margins compared to retail cabinet deployments. The company also continues its M&A strategy, including recent acquisitions of Verizon data centers and Metronode in Australia, expanding its global footprint.

title: Moody’s Downgrades Teva Bond Rating to “Junk”
summary: Moody's Investors Service downgraded Teva Pharmaceutical Industries Ltd.'s bond rating to "junk" due to the company's significant debt load, following Fitch Ratings Inc. which made a similar move in November. The generic drugmaker is carrying approximately $32 billion in debt, largely from its 2016 acquisition of Allergan’s generic business, and has been undertaking various restructuring efforts including asset sales, workforce reductions, and dividend halts to manage its financial challenges. Both Moody's and Fitch cite severe earnings erosion from generic competition, especially for Copaxone, and high execution risk in Teva's cost restructuring.

title: HYDW Stock Fund Price and Chart — AMEX:HYDW
summary: The article provides a detailed overview of the Xtrackers Low Beta High Yield Bond ETF (HYDW), including its current price, key statistics like AUM and dividend yield, and historical performance. It also explains the fund's investment strategy, structure, and answers frequently asked questions about ETFs and HYDW's specifics.

title: HYUP Stock Fund Price and Chart — AMEX:HYUP
summary: This article provides a comprehensive overview of the HYUP Xtrackers High Beta High Yield Bond ETF, including its price performance, key statistics like AUM and dividend yield, and detailed fund information. It also covers technical analysis, seasonal trends, and answers frequently asked questions about ETFs and HYUP's specifics.

title: Bitcoin Investment Trust Announces Stock Split
summary: Grayscale Investments, LLC, the sponsor of the Bitcoin Investment Trust (OTCQX: GBTC), announced a 91-for-1 stock split. Shareholders of record on January 22, 2018, will receive 90 additional shares for each share held, with the split becoming effective on January 26, 2018. Following the split, the Trust is projected to have 174,410,600 shares outstanding.

title: iShares filed for the iShares Long-Term National Muni Bond ETF
summary: iShares has filed for the iShares Long-Term National Muni Bond ETF. This ETF aims to track the investment results of an index composed of investment-grade U.S. municipal bonds with maturities of fifteen years or more, specifically the S&P 15+ Year National AMT-Free Municipal Bond Index. The filing did not disclose fees or tickers.

title: Black Construction executive wins award
summary: Leonard Kaae Sr., senior vice president and general manager of Black Construction Corp., was named the 2017 Guam Business Magazine Executive of the Year. The award recognizes his nearly four decades of leadership and significant contributions to numerous million-dollar projects across the Pacific Rim, including major infrastructure developments in Guam. Black Construction, under Kaae's management, has received national and regional accolades for its construction excellence.

title: GVIP ETF-Preis und Chart — AMEX:GVIP
summary: This article provides a detailed overview of the GVIP Goldman Sachs Hedge Industry VIP ETF (AMEX:GVIP), including its current price, performance metrics, fund details, and technical analysis. It covers key statistics like assets under management, dividend yield, expense ratio, and fund composition, along with answers to frequently asked questions about ETFs and GVIP.

title: Building smart mobility ecosystem
summary: Motorola Solutions' China unit, led by general manager Lily Fu, is strategically aligning itself with China's economic transformation. The company is evolving from a critical communications equipment manufacturer into an integrated solution provider, focusing on smart mobility and integrating technologies like AI, cloud computing, and big data. Motorola aims to leverage these advancements to enhance public safety and working efficiency, with a strong focus on increasing R&D and innovation in China.

title: First Solar to put new factory into operation before 2018 end
summary: First Solar is accelerating its recruitment efforts to launch operations at its new Ho Chi Minh City factory in Q4 2018. The company is investing an additional $360 million, bringing its total investment to $830 million for two factories that will produce 2.4GW Series 6 modules annually. This expansion will create 950 jobs and begin preliminary module production of its advanced thin-film PV Series 6 product by the end of 2018.

title: URANIUM: NexGen confirms multiple broad zones as high as 6.8% at South Arrow
summary: NexGen Energy has released assay results for 31 holes in the South Arrow zone of its Rook I uranium project, revealing multiple broad zones of high-grade uranium mineralization. The South Arrow zone features shallow, sub-parallel stacked mineralized shears with significant uranium oxide percentages, including some assays reaching up to 6.79% U3O8. The company is advancing with technical programs to support a pre-feasibility study slated for Q3 2018.

title: Pesticides Manufacturer Adama Raised $240 Million on Shenzhen Exchange
summary: Pesticides manufacturer Adama Agricultural Solutions Ltd. has raised $240 million through a private placement on the Shenzhen A-share market. The company plans to use these funds to build a formulation plant in China and expand existing manufacturing facilities in Israel, Brazil, and the U.S. Adama, acquired by ChemChina Group in 2011 and merged with Hubei Sanonda Co. Ltd. in 2017, markets crop-protection products in over 100 countries.

title: PSE buys SMC shares in PDSHC
summary: The Philippine Stock Exchange (PSE) has agreed to acquire San Miguel Corp.’s (SMC) four percent stake in Philippine Dealing System Holdings Corp. (PDSHC), which operates the Philippine Dealing & Exchange Corp. (PDex). This acquisition is part of PSE's broader plan to merge with PDEx to strengthen the Philippine capital market and follows similar transactions PSE entered into with other entities last year. The purchase is contingent on regulatory approvals, including from the Securities and Exchange Commission.

title: Broadridge Financial creates international division
summary: Broadridge Financial Solutions Inc. has established Broadridge International, a new division to manage and grow its business operations outside of North America. The Lake Success-based company, which generated the majority of its $4 billion revenue from North America last year, appointed Tom Carey to lead the international division. This move aligns with Broadridge's core strategy for international expansion.

title: A year after Trump deal, Carrier plant announces 2nd round of layoffs
summary: A year after President Trump's deal to save jobs at Carrier Corp., the Indianapolis plant announced a second round of layoffs, cutting 215 positions. This follows 340 job cuts in July, despite the initial agreement to prevent plant closure and save 800 furnace production jobs. The article also highlights how other companies are using tax savings for employee benefits, while automation continues to pose a threat to manufacturing jobs.

title: Manitowoc Company's final exit from community marks end of an era
summary: Manitowoc Company is relocating its corporate headquarters to Milwaukee, marking the end of an era for the Manitowoc community which had been home to the company since 1902. The move, following the closure of its manufacturing plant a year prior, has drawn mixed reactions from local leaders and business owners who acknowledge the loss of jobs but also see opportunity in the sale of the former headquarters to Investors Community Bank. Community leaders emphasize the need for diversification and retaining young talent to bolster the local economy.

title: Colorado pension fund sues 9 banks over alleged Canadian rate manipulation
summary: A Colorado pension fund has filed a lawsuit against nine banks, alleging manipulation of the Canadian Dollar Offered Rate (CDOR). This legal action highlights concerns about potential rigging of key financial benchmarks by large institutions. The suit seeks to address the alleged financial damage caused by these manipulative practices.

title: McDonald’s to further expand footprint in PH
summary: McDonald's Philippines, through its master franchise holder Golden Arches Development Corp., plans continued expansion in 2018, aiming to surpass 600 stores nationwide. The company, a venture with Alliance Global Group Inc., is optimistic due to a strong economy and growing middle class. Golden Arches also announced a partnership with PLDT Inc.’s PayMaya to accept card and QR code payments in an effort to adapt to the changing market.

title: These Internet Stocks Are Red Hot
summary: Despite rapid growth in stock price and concerns over inflated valuations, Morgan Stanley analyst Brian Nowak identifies nine hot tech stocks, including Alphabet, Facebook, and Amazon, that are expected to continue their strong performance in 2018 and beyond. The article details growth projections, financial figures, and specific catalysts for each company, emphasizing innovation, market dominance, and strategic investments as key drivers of their continued success in the internet sector.

title: Exclusive - U.S. lawmakers urge AT&T to cut commercial ties with Huawei: sources
summary: U.S. lawmakers are pressuring AT&T Inc. to sever commercial ties with Chinese phone maker Huawei Technologies Co Ltd and to oppose China Mobile Ltd's entry into the U.S. market, citing national security concerns. This move follows the Trump administration's harder stance on China and previous efforts by lawmakers to block AT&T's plans to offer Huawei handsets. Concerns center on the potential for Chinese government intelligence services to access user data from Huawei devices.

title: Veteran investor sees ‘giant opportunity’ in natural gas partnerships
summary: Veteran investor Mark J. Grant, chief global strategist at B. Riley/FBR/Wunderlich Securities, sees a significant opportunity in natural gas partnerships, particularly closed-end funds. He identifies five favorite closed-end funds with yields up to 13.8% and advocates for a conservative income-focused investment strategy. Grant recently joined the firm after 43 years in the financial industry.

title: Veteran investor sees ‘giant opportunity’ in natural gas partnerships
summary: Veteran investor Mark J. Grant, chief global strategist at B. Riley/FBR/Wunderlich Securities, sees a "giant opportunity" in natural gas partnerships for income-seeking investors. He recommends closed-end funds that invest in pipeline partnerships, noting some have yields as high as 13.8%. Grant shared his five favorite plays in the industry during an interview on January 10th.

summary: Mark J. Grant, chief global strategist at B. Riley/FBR/Wunderlich Securities, identifies a "giant opportunity" for income-seeking investors in natural gas partnerships, specifically closed-end funds with high yields. title: Veteran investor sees ‘giant opportunity’ in natural gas partnerships

He revealed five of his top picks, which offer yields up to 13.8%, and described a conservative income-focused strategy for investors. Grant recently joined the firm after 43 years in the financial industry.

title: Ford plans $11 billion investment, 40 electrified vehicles by 2022
summary: Ford Motor Co. announced a significant increase in its electric vehicle investment plan to $11 billion by 2022, aiming to introduce 40 hybrid and fully electric vehicles. This move is a sharp increase from a previous $4.5 billion target and reflects a broader industry trend towards electrification driven by regulatory pressures and the success of companies like Tesla. Ford also plans to electrify its mainstream and iconic vehicles, including a hybrid F-150 truck and a high-performance electric utility vehicle, and will cut $14 billion in costs over five years by shifting away from sedans and internal combustion engines.

title: Chevron Plans to Return to Iraq's Kurdistan
summary: Chevron Corp. plans to resume drilling in Iraq's Kurdistan region after temporarily halting operations in October. The U.S. oil major will drill the Sarta 3 well north of Erbil as tensions between the semi-autonomous region and the federal government abate.

title: Citigroup reports $18 billion loss on one-time tax items
summary: Citigroup reported an $18 billion quarterly loss due to one-time charges related to a new U.S. tax law, despite adjusted earnings beating Wall Street expectations. While the bank faced significant hits from the tax changes, management anticipates long-term benefits, including a lower tax rate and the potential to lift financial performance targets. The bank's shares rose, and consumer banking growth helped offset weaknesses in institutional business.

title: Drugmaker Agilent is hiring dozens for new Colorado plant
summary: Agilent Technologies Inc. is hiring dozens of people for its new Colorado plant, highlighting the complexity of the construction but also the strong technical skill and trades available in the region. The article quotes a representative discussing the challenges and successes of building the new facility.

title: Apple accelerates US investment and job creation
summary: Apple announced plans to contribute over $350 billion to the US economy over the next five years, fueled by repatriation tax payments, capital expenditures, and increased spending with domestic suppliers. This initiative is expected to create over 20,000 new jobs, establish a new Apple campus, and expand Apple's Advanced Manufacturing Fund to $5 billion. The company also highlighted its commitment to STEM education and preparing students for the app economy.

title: Familia Hurtado Berger subasta acciones secundarias Serie B de Embotelladora Andina
summary: The Hurtado Berger family, a controlling shareholder of Embotelladora Andina S.A., auctioned secondary Series B shares on the Santiago Stock Exchange, generating USD 199 million. The offering saw demand exceed supply 6.1 times, with investor orders surpassing USD 1.215 billion. Legal advisors included Grasty Quintana Majlis & Cía. for the sellers and internal legal teams for JP Morgan Corredores de Bolsa and Banchile Corredores de Bolsa, which coordinated the offer.

title: FDA works to ease IV shortages after Hurricane Maria
summary: The FDA is actively working to alleviate IV saline and amino acid drug shortages in the U.S. that resulted from Hurricane Maria's impact on Puerto Rico in September 2017, exacerbated by a severe flu season. Measures include importing products from abroad, approving new suppliers, and extending expiration dates of existing products. While the situation is improving with manufacturing sites regaining power, the FDA acknowledges the production situation remains "fragile."

title: The Wendy's Company Completes $925 Million Securitized Financing Facility
summary: The Wendy's Company announced that its subsidiary completed a $925 million securitized financing facility. This facility includes the sale of $450 million in Class A-2-I Notes and $475 million in Class A-2-II Notes, with anticipated repayment dates in March 2025 and March 2028, respectively. The net proceeds will be used to prepay existing debt, cover transaction costs, and for general corporate purposes.

title: Auburn welcomes new Boeing training center
summary: Boeing Auburn celebrated the grand opening of its Workforce Readiness Center, the site's first new building in 25 years, dedicated to enhancing the skills of Boeing Fabrication employees. The two-story, 71,000-square-foot building, costing about $17 million, will become a hub for teaching new skills in robotics, programming, and manufacturing, and will also house Auburn's medical clinic. This center aims to help recruit, develop, and retain employees critical to Boeing's long-term success and maintains the community's status as a critical hub in the supply chain.

title: Globus Maritime Files For Stock Shelf Of Up To $50 Mln - SEC Filing
summary: Globus Maritime Ltd. has filed for a stock shelf offering of up to $50 million, according to an SEC filing. Additionally, a selling shareholder may offer up to 15 million of the company's common shares.

title: Why Did Chipotle Mexican Grill, Inc. Shares Lose 23% in 2017?
summary: Despite positive financial performance including increased revenue and EPS, Chipotle Mexican Grill's stock fell 23% in 2017 due to lingering public wariness over past food safety issues. The article suggests that only time and consistent execution will allow the company to fully recover from its reputation challenges.

title: The Burrito Index: Let's talk about the relative price of Burrito Bowls.
summary: This article introduces "The Burrito Index" which examines the varying prices of Chipotle Burrito Bowls across different U.S. cities. It highlights significant price discrepancies, such as a 28% difference between New York City and Jacksonville, Florida, even after accounting for cost of living. The index aims to analyze these relative costs, similar to The Economist's Big Mac Index, considering factors like local labor, supply, real estate, and market competition.

title: BLCN Stock Fund Price and Chart — NASDAQ:BLCN
summary: This article provides comprehensive information about the Siren NexGen Economy ETF (BLCN), one of the first ETFs focused on blockchain technology. It details the fund's price, performance, key statistics, holdings, and management style. The article also includes news, ideas, technical analysis, and a frequently asked questions section to help investors understand the ETF.

title: What the US can learn from Sweden about how to launch a bitcoin fund
summary: This article examines how Sweden successfully launched bitcoin exchange-traded products years ago, offering a model for the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC), which has rejected all bitcoin ETF filings. The key difference lies in Sweden's use of exchange-traded notes (ETNs) rather than exchange-traded funds (ETFs) to track bitcoin, despite initial SEC concerns over liquidity and valuation. These Swedish ETNs have attracted significant investment and demonstrate a viable pathway for providing U.S. investors access to bitcoin markets.

title: Alcoa reports deeper 4Q loss as restructuring continues
summary: Alcoa Corp. reported a wider fourth-quarter loss of $196 million, or $1.06 per share, as it continues restructuring efforts. The company missed analyst expectations but announced plans to freeze its pension and move 800 employees to a defined contribution retirement plan to strengthen its foundation amid favorable markets. Alcoa also noted a $22 million charge due to tax reforms but anticipates little impact on 2018 results, swinging to a 2017 net income of $217 million.

title: Early returns: 2018's top-performing bank stocks
summary: This article highlights the top-performing large and mid-cap bank stocks at the beginning of 2018, based on stock price gains over 20 trading days ending January 12. It details 12 banks that significantly outperformed the NASDAQ Bank Index, providing company specifics, market capitalization, and key financial insights or recent news for each. The analysis from FIG Partners points out geographical concentrations of these high-performing banks in warmer states like California, Texas, Georgia, Arkansas, Florida, and Virginia.

title: GasLog Partners LP Announces Closing of its Public Offering
summary: GasLog Partners LP announced the closing of its public offering of 4,600,000 8.200% Series B Cumulative Redeemable Perpetual Fixed to Floating Rate Preference Units, including units purchased by underwriters. The offering generated approximately $111.0 million in net proceeds, which the Partnership intends to use for general partnership purposes, possibly including future acquisitions, debt repayment, and capital expenditures. The Series B Preference Units will be listed on the New York Stock Exchange under the symbol GLOP PR B.

title: Stock Market's Crucial End-of-Day Auctions Set for Shakeup
summary: The SEC has approved a proposal by Cboe Global Markets to change how end-of-day stock auctions are handled, allowing traders to buy or sell shares at the daily closing price without incurring fees from the NYSE or Nasdaq. This move is seen as a significant challenge to the dominance of NYSE and Nasdaq in setting final end-of-day prices for thousands of stocks. The decision aims to introduce more competition and potentially reduce costs for traders engaging in these crucial auctions.

title: BlackRock CEO Larry Fink Wants a Kinder, Gentler Capitalism. He Should Look At His Own Investments.
summary: This article criticizes BlackRock CEO Larry Fink's call for socially responsible capitalism by highlighting BlackRock's significant investments in private prisons, fossil fuels, and major banks accused of questionable practices. It details BlackRock's substantial holdings in companies like GEO Group, CoreCivic, Exxon Mobil, Range Resources, Anadarko, Dominion Energy, Cloud Peak Energy, Goldman Sachs, and Wells Fargo, questioning the sincerity of Fink's shareholder activism given these investments. The author suggests Fink should examine BlackRock's own portfolio to align its actions with his stated goal of positive societal contribution.

title: Heico Corp Share Prices Adjusted For Stock Split
summary: Heico Corp's Class A Common Stock and Common Stock prices have been adjusted to reflect a previously announced 5-for-4 stock split. Trading commenced on a "post-split" basis, with prices automatically adjusting downward by 25% from the NYSE closing price on January 17.

title: Facebook names American Express CEO Kenneth Chenault, first African-American, to all-white board
summary: Facebook has appointed Kenneth Chenault, the former CEO of American Express, to its board of directors, making him the first African-American director on the previously all-white board. This appointment follows years of recruitment efforts by Facebook CEO Mark Zuckerberg and civil rights leader Jesse Jackson's lobbying for increased diversity within Silicon Valley companies. Chenault's addition is seen as a move to address the striking lack of people of color in executive and board positions in the tech industry and leverage his expertise in customer service, direct commerce, and brand building.

title: What triggered the oil price plunge of 2014-2016 and why it failed to deliver an economic impetus in eight charts
summary: The 2014-2016 oil price collapse, driven by a supply glut from booming U.S. shale oil production, failed to significantly boost global economic growth as anticipated. This was due to low responsiveness of economic activity in key oil-importing emerging markets, a contraction in U.S. energy investment, and a slowdown in oil-exporting economies. The article provides eight charts illustrating these factors, highlighting the need for greater diversification among oil exporters and the long-term implications of the price plunge.

title: Big Oil CEO: Hiring Women Isn't the Problem, Keeping Them Is
summary: ConocoPhillips CEO Ryan Lance states that while the oil industry has improved in hiring women, retaining them, particularly those raising families, remains a significant challenge. He notes that women constitute a quarter of Conoco's executive leadership and 40% of its board, and despite an increase in female and minority workers among younger employees, the long-term retention issue persists.

title: U.S. Dredging Industry Invests in American Workers, New State-of-the-Art Technology Delivers Four New Vessels for Critical Infrastructure Projects
summary: The American Maritime Partnership highlighted the U.S. dredging industry's commitment to building and maintaining navigation channels through investments in new technology and American workers. The industry recently delivered four state-of-the-art vessels, representing over $310 million in new construction, supporting the U.S. shipyard industrial base and critical infrastructure projects. These vessels, including the MAGDALEN, ELLIS ISLAND, and ROBERT M. WHITE, enhance capacity for complex operations while adhering to high environmental and safety standards.

title: Tax Reform: Implications for the US High Yield Bond Market
summary: The Tax Cuts and Jobs Act of 2017 introduced changes that are expected to be a net positive for the U.S. high-yield bond market, primarily due to a reduction in the corporate tax rate from 35% to 21%. While interest expense deductibility is limited, many high-yield companies will benefit due to their current interest expense to EBITDA ratios being below the threshold where the tax changes would be neutral or negative. An analysis of a high-yield bond ETF shows that only a small portion of its holdings are likely to be negatively impacted by these changes.

title: US Bancorp’s Richard Davis Retiring as Chairman of the Board
summary: Richard Davis, former CEO of US Bancorp, announced his retirement as chairman of the board, effective in April, with CEO Andy Cecere set to replace him. Davis led US Bancorp to become the nation's fifth-largest commercial bank and was instrumental in bringing U.S. Bank Stadium and the 2018 Super Bowl to Minneapolis. During his tenure as CEO from 2006 to 2016, revenue increased by 49 percent, from $13.6 billion to $21.3 billion, as the bank navigated the Great Recession by avoiding risky investments.

title: Wyndham to buy La Quinta hotel business for $1.95 billion
summary: Wyndham Worldwide Corp announced it would acquire La Quinta Holdings Inc's hotel operations for $1.95 billion, adding nearly 900 mid-scale to economy locations and bringing its total brands to 21. This acquisition is expected to make Wyndham the third-largest hotel group globally by room count, surpassing InterContinental, and is seen as credit-positive for Wyndham due to La Quinta's strong performance in the mid-scale segments. The deal precedes Wyndham's planned spin-off into two separate companies and involves La Quinta spinning off its real estate assets into CorePoint Lodging Inc.

title: Watch MOO ETF Milks Returns
summary: The article highlights the VanEck Vectors Agribusiness ETF (MOO), noting its unique position as the first ETF to track global agriculture companies. While its performance traditionally correlated with grain prices, the ETF has experienced a significant breakout over the past two years, as explained by Bloomberg's Scarlet Fu.

title: MGIC Investment Corp Q4 Earnings Advance 49%
summary: MGIC Investment Corp (MTG) reported a significant increase in its Q4 earnings, with profit rising to $160.65 million, or $0.43 per share, up 49% from the previous year. This performance exceeded analysts' expectations of $0.28 per share. The company also saw a modest revenue increase of 1.9% to $271.50 million for the quarter.

title: Americold Realty prices upsized IPO at $16, the high end of the range
summary: Americold Realty Trust, the world's largest cold-storage REIT backed by Yucaipa Companies, successfully priced its upsized IPO at $16 per share, the high end of its target range, raising $725 million. The company increased the offering to 45.3 million shares, including additional primary shares, after initially planning to sell fewer. Americold Realty Trust will list on the NYSE under the symbol COLD, with BofA Merrill Lynch, J.P. Morgan, and RBC Capital Markets as lead managers.

title: Convenience Stores Are Getting Squeezed by Fast Food and Dollar Stores
summary: The U.S. convenience store industry is facing increasing pressure from various competitors, including fast-food restaurants, supermarkets, dollar stores, and Amazon.com Inc. This intense competition is impacting merchandise sales growth, which is the weakest since 2013, and is pushing gas-station retail chains towards consolidation and diversification of their offerings.

title: Will Liquid Alt ETFs Ever Take Off?
summary: This article explores the potential for liquid alternative ETFs to gain broader adoption among investors. It features an interview with Yasmin Dahya from J.P. Morgan Asset Management, who discusses how these ETFs aim to democratize access to hedge fund strategies at a lower cost and provide diversification in current market conditions. The discussion highlights the benefits of factor-driven alternative ETFs and the challenges they face in investor education and technology integration.

title: Fabory Group, Ronald Baarslag, general manager
summary: Fabory Group experienced significant growth in 2016-2017 driven by a focus on market share and economic growth, leading to warehouse expansion. The company is adapting to megatrends like digitization and increased demand for supply chain solutions, while also facing challenges such as a scarcity of digital talent and external pressures like raw material price fluctuations, new regulations, and geopolitical influences affecting the fastener market. These trends are expected to impact pricing and availability throughout 2018 and beyond.

title: Osceola Food Honored for its Work on the Industrial Tech Advisory Board
summary: Osceola Food has been honored for its collaboration with the Industrial Tech Advisory Board on a program designed to provide high school students with valuable trade skills. This initiative addresses the declining skilled workforce in Osceola, Iowa, and aims to develop a self-sustaining workforce for the future growth of the region. The program was recognized at the Osceola Chamber Main Street and Clarke County Development Corporation's annual dinner, attended by Iowa Governor Kim Reynolds and United States Senator Joni Ernst.

title: How CEO Jim Risoleo Maintains a Fresh Perspective After 20 Years at Host Hotels & Resorts
summary: Jim Risoleo, CEO of Host Hotels & Resorts Inc., discusses his first year as CEO after two decades with the company, sharing insights on maintaining a fresh perspective, the benefits of scale, the outlook for the lodging industry, and the role of technology in transforming hotels. He emphasizes the importance of a geographically diverse portfolio of iconic hotels and the company's strong financial position.

title: Yet another Blockchain ETF
summary: This article discusses several new ETF listings, including two S&P 500 trackers from Metaurus Advisors that separate capital growth and dividends, and First Trust's new Blockchain ETF (LEGR). It also briefly mentions new ETFs from Fubon in Taiwan focusing on China Policy Bank Bonds and Guangfa in China targeting media companies. The article provides details on the structure and investment strategies of these new funds.

title: Going Big: China’s Super-Sized Infrastructure
summary: China, as the largest steel-producing country, has undertaken numerous massive infrastructure projects to boost its economy and global trade. The article highlights several of these "super-sized" constructions, including the Three Gorges Dam, Beijing Capital International Airport, Jiaozhou Bay Bridge, Jiuquan Wind Power Base, New Century Global Center, and the Port of Shanghai. These projects demonstrate China's capacity for large-scale engineering and its use of steel to set world records, aiming for greater connectivity and economic prosperity.

title: Starbucks named fifth most admired company worldwide
summary: Starbucks has been recognized by Fortune magazine as the fifth most admired company worldwide and the number one company in the food and beverage industry for the 16th consecutive year. It is the only traditional brick-and-mortar retail business to make it into the top 10. The rankings are based on surveys of executives and securities analysts who rate companies on criteria such as innovation, financial soundness, and social responsibility.

title: Major US railroads warn Trump against derailing NAFTA

He noted an 8% boost for American workers and "substantially higher" corporate profits, anticipating over 4% economic growth next year. Charles Schwab also rewarded its employees with a $1,000 bonus due to the savings from the tax bill.

summary: Assurant, Inc. has announced it will utilize the $276.7 million net proceeds from a recent stock offering, along with other capital, to finance its $2.5 billion acquisition of TWG Holding, Ltd. The stock proceeds resulted from the sale of 2,875,000 shares of mandatory convertible preferred stock. These funds will also be used to refinance existing 2.50% Senior Notes due in 2018 and cover related expenses.

title: AutoNation signs deal to keep HQ in Fort Lauderdale, hire 95
summary: AutoNation has signed a deal to renew and expand its headquarters agreement with Stiles Corporation in Fort Lauderdale, also announcing plans to hire 95 new employees. This move continues AutoNation's presence in the city and reflects its ongoing operations and growth.

title: Why Do Active Managers Do Better in Some Periods Than Others?
summary: A Morningstar study investigates whether active managers' index-relative performance is influenced by their investment style, a concept known as Dunn's Law. The research suggests that while Dunn's Law has some merit, and style differences explain much of the variation in success rates, these success rates are often noisy and difficult to predict. The article concludes that attempting to time exposure between active and passive funds based on these fluctuating success rates is not advisable.

title: China Sells Stake in Blackstone as Deal Scene Turns Sour
summary: China Investment Corporation (C.I.C.), China's sovereign wealth fund, has sold its stake in Blackstone Group, signaling an end to an 11-year investment that symbolized early economic cooperation between the U.S. and China. This divestment occurs amid a deteriorating relationship between the two countries, marked by U.S. officials taking a harder stance on Chinese investments and President Trump's trade policies. Despite the sale, Blackstone emphasized its continuing relationship with C.I.C. through other investment funds.

title: Las nueve empresas argentinas destacadas entre las mejores "multilatinas"

While Argentina shows improvement with more companies on the list compared to 2009, BCG notes the country remains underrepresented relative to its GDP size.

title: Incyte study could bring lessons for cancer immunotherapy
summary: A Phase 3 study combining Merck & Co.'s Keytruda with Incyte Corp.'s experimental drug epacadostat in metastatic melanoma patients is highly anticipated. The trial's results, expected in May, could significantly impact Incyte's market capitalization and offer crucial insights into optimal cancer immunotherapy combinations. Success would position epacadostat as a key partner for PD-1/L1 blockers, particularly in melanoma, while failure would temper enthusiasm for IDO inhibitors.

title: If Broadcom-Qualcomm deal can’t pass Trump’s test, what can?
summary: President Donald Trump blocked Broadcom Ltd.'s takeover attempt of Qualcomm Inc., citing national security concerns. This intervention could have a significant chilling effect on future foreign deals for U.S. tech companies and American companies' bids for foreign rivals. The blocked merger would have been the largest tech merger in history.

title: Prudential to split into two companies to target Asia
summary: Prudential plans to split its business into two FTSE 100 companies: one focused on the UK and Europe (M&G Prudential) and the other on its high-growth US and Asian operations (Prudential plc). Both companies will be headquartered in London, listed on the London Stock Exchange, and shareholders will hold shares in both new entities. This strategic move aims to allow each business to better concentrate on its respective markets and capitalize on growth opportunities.

summary: China Investment Corp (CIC), China's sovereign wealth fund, has sold its equity stake in U.S. private equity firm Blackstone Group LP, ending an 11-year investment. Despite the equity sale, CIC and Blackstone continue to cooperate in other areas such as real estate, hedge funds, and direct investments.

These raises occurred amidst various new revelations of customer abuses, including charges for unneeded auto insurance and improper mortgage fees.
