title: HarborOne buys RI bank Coastway for $125.6M
summary: HarborOne Bancorp Inc. has acquired Rhode Island-based Coastway Community Bank for $125.6 million in cash. The acquisition is expected to close in the second half of the year, with Coastway stockholders receiving $28.25 per share. This deal will make the merged HarborOne-Coastway the 12th largest community bank by assets in New England, with 65 locations across four states.

title: Bridgewater Bancshares Stock Jumps in Debut on Nasdaq Exchange
summary: Bridgewater Bancshares Inc. saw its stock jump on its debut on the Nasdaq stock exchange, with shares finishing at $12.85 after two days of public trading. The Bloomington-based bank raised $78.7 million in its initial public offering, making it the first banking company from Minnesota to go public in nearly 25 years. Bridgewater has experienced rapid growth, increasing its assets from $1 billion in 2016 to $1.6 billion by the end of 2017, largely attributed to its commercial real estate lending business.

title: Behind the Wheel: Case IH and New Holland mark the start of Brazil’s soybean harvest
summary: Case IH and New Holland Agriculture are initiating Brazil's soybean harvest, a critical event given that soybeans constitute over 50% of the country's grain production and significantly contribute to the development of its rural Midwest. The companies, responsible for roughly 50% of Brazil's soybean harvest, which amounted to 170 million tons in 2017, are highlighted in a "Behind the Wheel" webisode. This content showcases the people and advanced harvesting technology that have transformed the soybean industry and fostered economic development in regions like Canarana, Mato Grosso.

title: Compass investigation: Cayman’s water – Where it comes from, where it goes …
summary: This article investigates the source and distribution of fresh water in the Cayman Islands, detailing how desalination technology and reverse osmosis plants provide potable water to the growing population. It highlights the roles of Cayman Water and the Water Authority in managing the water supply, the history of water provision, and the advanced methods used to ensure water quality and resilience against natural disasters. The article also touches on the economic efficiency of water management in Cayman compared to other regions facing water crises.

title: Ford, Once a Leader in the S.U.V. Race, Aims to Catch Up (Published 2018)
summary: Ford Motor, once a leader in the SUV market, is now making a concerted effort to regain its position by introducing numerous new SUV models over the next three years. The company plans to make SUVs and pickup trucks account for 90 percent of its North American vehicle production by 2020, with a focus on hybrid, electric, and off-road variants. Ford also aims to cut costs by streamlining vehicle development and reducing the number of basic component architectures.

title: Powering a Green Future with Lithium Batteries
summary: The market for lithium batteries is projected to reach USD 40 billion by 2024, driven by advancements in electric vehicles (EVs) and other electronic devices. Innovations like solid-state and flexible lithium-ion batteries are addressing challenges such as charging time, weight, and size. POSCO is investing in sustainable lithium extraction, with its PosLX plant producing 2,500 tons annually using advanced, eco-friendly technology.

Technical analysis suggests continued downward pressure on the stock, with foreign selling a major contributing factor.

title: Unilever moves HQ to Rotterdam
summary: Unilever announced it will scrap its London corporate headquarters, making Rotterdam its sole legal home, a move seen as a blow to post-Brexit investment efforts in the UK. The Anglo-Dutch company plans to simplify its dual-headed structure into a single Dutch legal entity, though it maintains the decision is unrelated to Brexit but rather aimed at creating a "simpler, more agile and more focused business." The company's new structure will see two divisions headquartered in London and one in Rotterdam, and it will continue to be listed in London, Amsterdam, and New York.

title: Why Unilever Is Abandoning its London Base for Headquarters in the Netherlands
summary: Unilever is consolidating its headquarters in the Netherlands, abandoning its U.K. base after nearly a century. This move simplifies its dual-headquarters structure and follows an unsolicited takeover bid from Kraft Heinz Co., making mergers and acquisitions easier. Despite denial of a Brexit connection, the decision places its headquarters within the EU and leverages Dutch takeover laws that offer stronger protection against hostile approaches.

title: Brazil
summary: Earthworks supports frontline community groups and social movement organizations in Brazil advocating for safer tailings disposal facilities and justice for mining company crimes. The organization highlights the dangers of tailings dams in Brazil, which have caused numerous fatalities and environmental devastation, particularly in Minas Gerais and the Amazon. Earthworks works with communities to address past disasters and prevent future ones, including stopping the construction of new damaging mining projects.

title: Ventas Resuscitates South Street Landing
summary: Ventas, Inc. played a key role in the $220 million redevelopment of South Street Landing in Providence, Rhode Island, transforming a former power station into a dynamic academic and professional hub. This project, a collaboration between multiple learning institutions, city and state entities, and developers Ventas and Wexford Science Technology, LLC, is the first phase of revitalizing Providence’s historic Jewelry District into an innovation hub. The redevelopment leveraged historic tax credits and aims to foster economic growth, improve healthcare, and create jobs through a public-private partnership model.

title: Wells Fargo CEO slams criticism on his 35% pay hike
summary: Wells Fargo CEO Timothy J. Sloan defended his $4.6 million pay raise, bringing his total compensation to $17.4 million, amidst ongoing investigations into widespread consumer abuses at the bank. Sloan argued the raise reflected his full year as CEO in 2017 and the challenges faced by the company, noting he declined a bonus. He addressed the bank's "painful mistakes" and efforts to rebuild trust, emphasizing improved customer loyalty and reduced employee turnover despite continued regulatory scrutiny over past scandals.

title: Why every investor should be terrified by the slide in Home Depot stock
summary: The article highlights concerns surrounding the recent downturn in Home Depot stock, despite a strong performance over the past decade. It points out that while consumer spending is high and tax cuts theoretically boost the economy, the housing market, where Home Depot thrives, appears to have hit a wall.

title: FedEx Announces Billion-Dollar Expansion at Memphis Headquarters
summary: FedEx Corp. is investing over $1 billion to modernize its Memphis, Tenn.-based headquarters, with construction set to begin next year and completion expected by 2025. This expansion, entirely funded by FedEx, includes a new sort facility, state-of-the-art sorting systems, a bulk truckload building, and improved handling for oversize shipments. The project aims to benefit current and future employees and reinforce FedEx's commitment to Tennessee, where it is the largest employer.

title: Adobe earnings: $100 billion valuation to get its first big test
summary: Adobe Systems Inc. is facing its first major test as a $100 billion company with its upcoming fiscal first-quarter earnings report. Analysts are looking for continued strong organic revenue growth, specifically 20% or more from its cloud model, to justify its current valuation. The company's shares have surged 370% since it transitioned to a cloud-subscription model in late 2013.

title: Solid Biosciences Clinical Trial Put on Hold by FDA, Sends Share Price Tumbling
summary: Solid Biosciences (NASDAQ: SLDB) saw its share price plummet after the FDA placed a hold on its phase 1 IGNITE DMD trial for SGT-001, a gene therapy for Duchenne muscular dystrophy. The hold was prompted by negative laboratory findings including a decrease in platelet count, reduction in red blood cell count, and evidence of complement activation. Despite the setback, the company plans to work with the FDA to resume the trial, and an analyst downgraded the stock to a "sell."

summary: A study commissioned by AES and ordered by the EPA revealed that coal ash from AES’s plant in Guayama, Puerto Rico, is contaminating groundwater with radioactive materials, arsenic, chromium, selenium, and molybdenum. LafargeHolcim Ltd. is also highlighted for its application of circular economy principles in developing aggneo, a recycled concrete-derived aggregate, contributing to a goal of reusing 80 million tons of process material annually.

summary: FedEx announced a $1 billion investment to upgrade and expand its Memphis, Tennessee, processing hub due to growth in e-commerce. This follows a larger $1.5 billion investment in its Indianapolis hub, highlighting the company's strategy to adapt to increasing package volumes and oversized shipments.

summary: The article details Knife River Corp.'s investment in an Elrus portable crushing plant for its Angell Quarry in Portland, Oregon, to capitalize on anticipated aggregate business growth. The system has improved efficiency, safety, and environmental impact while producing high-quality aggregate.

summary: Sayreville's planned $2.5 billion Riverton waterfront project aims to create a new mixed-use community, transforming the former NL Industries site into a "town within a town." Developed by North American Properties, the project will include retail, office, residential, and hotel spaces, with a groundbreaking expected later this year and completion over a decade. The developers are addressing community concerns regarding traffic, schools, and the environmental remediation of the site.

title: Contractor change at OxyChem facilities affects up to 548 jobs

summary: Cummins India Ltd (CIL) plans to invest Rs2,000 crore in capital expenditure over the next five years to expand operations and consolidate its position in the automotive and industrial engine segments and the genset market. The company, part of the $13.2 billion Cummins Inc., aims to increase its manufacturing plants near Pune from three to 9-10 in the coming years and is focusing on new product development, including a new 8.9-liter engine for commercial vehicles. A one-time $6.9 billion charge related to U.S. tax law also led to the company being in the red for its fiscal third quarter.

summary: Cloud security company Zscaler went public on Friday, March 16, 2018, with its stock value more than doubling on its first trading day, reaching a market cap of $3.87 billion. Zscaler's platform inspecting network traffic without slowing applications signals a shift towards targeted solutions in an age of cloud applications.

title: General Mills Quarterly Dividend Declared
summary: The General Mills Board of Directors declared a quarterly dividend of $0.49 per share. This dividend is payable on May 1, 2018, to shareholders of record as of April 10, 2018. General Mills and its predecessor company have a 119-year history of uninterrupted dividend payments.

title: Zscaler IPO: 5 things to know about the first big tech IPO of 2018
summary: MarketWatch reports on Zscaler Inc.'s IPO, highlighting it as the first major tech unicorn to go public in 2018. The company, founded by CEO Jay Chaudhry, specializes in cloud security software for businesses. Zscaler is expected to reach an initial valuation of over $1.5 billion.

title: Heron Therapeutics preps NDA as its long-acting anesthetic sails through phase 3
summary: Heron Therapeutics' long-acting local anesthetic, HTX-011, successfully met all primary and key secondary endpoints in two phase 3 trials for bunion-correcting surgery and hernia repair patients. The drug significantly reduced pain intensity and opioid use for 72 hours post-surgery compared to placebo and bupivacaine. Heron Therapeutics plans to submit a New Drug Application in the second half of 2018, aiming for HTX-011 to impact the opioid crisis and achieve peak sales of $545M.

title: A small oil field in Oklahoma is seeing big bets from producers
summary: The Meramec formation within Oklahoma's STACK region is attracting significant new drilling and investment from oil producers like Devon Energy and Marathon Oil, as the rising output makes it competitive with the Permian Basin. This increased interest is driven by rising production levels and soaring land costs in the Permian, though potential challenges include earthquake concerns and slightly higher break-even prices.

title: Kroger to stop selling guns of all kinds
summary: Kroger announced its decision to stop selling all firearms and ammunition at its 132 Fred Meyer stores, citing "softening consumer demand" and an effort to optimize store space. This follows previous restrictions and a recent response to events like the Parkland shooting. The firearms category represented approximately $7 million in annual revenue for the company, with sales continuing to decline.

title: AutoZone among retailers sending Trump letter with tariff concerns
summary: Memphis-based AutoZone was among 25 companies that signed a letter to President Trump expressing concerns about proposed tariffs. The letter argues that broadly applied tariffs on everyday consumer products would negatively impact working families. This action highlights retailers' anxieties regarding the potential economic consequences of trade protectionism.

title: BofA Dials Back on Some Stock Loans After $292 Million Loss
summary: Bank of America has completed its internal review of a $292 million loss related to troubled South African firm Steinhoff International Holdings NV. Following this loss, BofA has reduced its involvement in the type of stock-based loans that led to the financial setback. The loss stemmed from a loan to Steinhoff's former chairman, Christo Wiese, collateralized by company shares that subsequently plummeted in value due to accounting irregularities.

title: Salesforce Just Bought MuleSoft, an IT Company That Went Public Last Year
summary: Salesforce has announced its largest acquisition to date, agreeing to buy MuleSoft for $6.5 billion in a cash and stock deal. MuleSoft, which went public last year, specializes in connecting business applications and IT infrastructure. This acquisition will help Salesforce expand beyond its core sales software and enhance its Integration Cloud offering.

title: Oracle Corporation | $ORCL Stock | Shares Slide After Q3 Earnings Report
summary: Oracle Corporation's shares experienced a significant drop after its third-quarter revenue failed to meet Wall Street estimates, despite adjusted earnings per share surpassing expectations. The decline worsened following a lower-than-expected fourth-quarter forecast. The company's Software-as-a-Service (SaaS) business revenue also missed analyst predictions, impacting overall financial performance.

title: The 80 Year Old Millennial
summary: A Prudential study reveals that millennials are less confident about their financial future than previous generations, largely believing they will need to work longer and that comfortable retirement may become a thing of the past. The study highlights millennials' concerns about job instability, the future of employer benefits, and the increasing role of technology in finance and healthcare, emphasizing their unique economic challenges and tech-first mindset.

title: Toro Purchases Commercial Lawn Care Equipment Maker L.T. Rich Products
summary: The Toro Company has acquired L.T. Rich Products, a manufacturer of commercial lawn care equipment, to expand its portfolio of spreaders, sprayers, aerators, and snow and ice equipment. L.T. Rich, known for its Z-Spray and Z-Plug brands, will continue to manufacture products from its Indiana facility for the near future. This acquisition follows Toro's minor investment in GreenSight Agronomics earlier in the year.

title: McDonald's Becomes the First Restaurant Company to Set Approved Science Based Target to Reduce Greenhouse Gas Emissions
summary: McDonald's announced a new strategy to reduce greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions, becoming the first restaurant company to set an approved science-based target. The company aims to prevent 150 million metric tons of GHG emissions by 2030 through initiatives across its supply chain, restaurants, and offices, focusing on beef production, energy use, packaging, and waste. This commitment involves working with franchisees and suppliers to achieve a 36% reduction in emissions related to restaurants and offices and a 31% reduction in emissions intensity across its supply chain from 2015 levels.

title: DTE’s $1B gas plant reaches full boil
summary: DTE Energy Co.'s proposal for a $1 billion natural gas plant to replace retiring coal units in Michigan has set off a bitter fight with clean energy advocates. Critics argue that DTE’s plan relies on faulty assumptions about renewable energy costs and technology, suggesting a carbon-free approach would be more economical and prudent. The Michigan Public Service Commission is set to decide on the contentious proposal by the end of April, with implications for the state’s energy future.

title: Why Investors Shouldn’t Panic About 3 Percent Treasury Bonds
summary: This article discusses investor fears surrounding the 10-year Treasury yield crossing the 3 percent mark, a level not seen since 2014. It explains that while rising rates reflect a strengthening economy and can impact mortgages and loan costs, experts like Jerry Paul and Jonathan Golub believe a 3 percent or even 3.5 percent yield is not a catastrophic tipping point for financial markets. Instead, they suggest that any significant market sell-off due to such rate increases would likely be a misunderstanding and an excellent buying opportunity.

title: Fiserv's stock gains after stock split goes into effect
summary: Fiserv Inc.'s stock saw gains after its 2-for-1 stock split went into effect following Monday's close. The financial services technology company's stock, which closed Monday at a pre-split price of $147.24, was trading about 1.2% above its post-split equivalent of $73.62 in premarket trade on Tuesday. This marks their second 2-for-1 split since December 2013, with the stock having rallied 26.2% over the past year compared to the S&P 500's 14.3% gain.

title: Electricity deal clinches $100M bitcoin mining operation in Medicine Hat
summary: The City of Medicine Hat has secured a $100 million bitcoin mining operation through a deal to supply electricity and lease land to Toronto-based Hut 8 Mining Corp. The company will construct new facilities, expanding its operating power to 60.7 megawatts and creating approximately 100 temporary and 42 ongoing jobs. This initiative is part of Medicine Hat's efforts to diversify its economy following the decline in oil and gas.

title: Oracle stock heads for worst day in nearly 5 years, analysts run for shelter after cloud bursts
summary: Shares of Oracle Corp. experienced their worst single-day percentage decline in nearly five years after disappointing quarterly results, particularly in its cloud-software business. The slowdown in cloud growth led to two downgrades and multiple price-target declines from Wall Street analysts. Oracle stock fell 9.0% and was the biggest percentage decliner in the S&P 500 index on Tuesday.

title: Exxon may build new Gulf Coast polypropylene facility
summary: Exxon Mobil Corp. is considering constructing a new polypropylene facility on the Gulf Coast, with potential startup as early as 2021. This consideration is part of a series of investments and projects Exxon Mobil is undertaking in the region and emerging markets. The article highlights other related Exxon Mobil activities including bringing a Houston-area project online and planning to triple Permian Basin production.

title: FedEx Reports Solid Quarter, Expands Walmart Deal
summary: FedEx Corp. reported strong fiscal third-quarter results, benefiting from the U.S. Tax Cuts and Jobs Act and solid performance from its FedEx Ground division. The company also announced a significant expansion of its partnership with Walmart, adding 500 office locations in stores over the next two years. Despite concerns about tariffs expressed by CEO Fred Smith, FedEx saw increased revenue and operating income in its Ground and Freight segments.

title: Peter G. Peterson, Blackstone's Co-Founder, Dies at 91
summary: Peter G. Peterson, the co-founder of Blackstone Group LP and a prominent Wall Street figure, has died at 91. He was known for rebuilding Lehman Bros. before co-founding the world's largest private-equity firm. Peterson passed away at his home in New York City.

title: iPhone: Designed in California but imported from China
summary: The article explores how Apple's iPhone, despite being designed in California, is assembled in China, significantly contributing to the US trade deficit with China. It highlights that while components come from various countries, current trade statistics count most of the manufacturing cost under China's exports. This complex global supply chain suggests that a US-China trade war could have wide-ranging economic damage.

title: Guess Inc Holiday Sales Beat Estimates
summary: Guess Inc reported holiday season quarterly revenue that surpassed analysts' estimates due to strong demand in Europe and Asia, leading to a nearly 12 percent rise in its shares. However, the company's net income attributable to Guess fell to $1.04 million from $6.6 million a year earlier, primarily impacted by a one-time charge of $47.9 million related to the new U.S. tax law.

title: The Price of M&A: After Gutting HP, Autonomy Strikes Again
summary: Shares of Micro Focus plunged 47% after its CEO resigned and the company dramatically revised down its revenue forecast, attributing the issues to its recent $8.8 billion acquisition of Hewlett Packard Enterprise Software, which included the problematic Autonomy. This event mirrors past difficulties with Autonomy, which HP had previously acquired and written off a significant portion of its value, leading to legal action against Autonomy executives. The article highlights how Wall Street benefits significantly from these M&A deals, regardless of the subsequent performance for investors.

title: Project finance getting more viable for energy storage, Moody’s says
summary: A new Moody's Investors Service report indicates that project finance is becoming increasingly viable for battery storage projects. Despite some unique characteristics, the risks associated with financing battery storage are broadly similar to conventional power projects, with the key credit risk being operation in accordance with design parameters. The viability of battery storage systems is improving due to falling costs, increased efficiency, and growing regulatory support, leading to an expected nine-fold growth in energy storage from 2017 to 2022.

title: New Orders Stoke the Fortunes at GE Transportation Fort Worth Locomotive Plant
summary: GE Transportation's Fort Worth locomotive plant is experiencing a resurgence in business due to new orders for refurbished and new locomotives from several railroads. This boost comes after a period of uncertainty for the plant, which had been facing a potential sale or spin-off of GE's locomotive division. The modernization program will also lead to increased hiring at the Fort Worth facility.

title: Pharma Giant Amgen Sends Its Estimated $350 Million U.S. Media Business to Hearts & Science
summary: Biotech company Amgen has selected Omnicom Media Group agency Hearts & Science as its media agency of record for its estimated $350 million U.S. media business. The decision followed a review launched in October, with Hearts & Science competing against Wavemaker and Starcom in the final rounds. Omnicom sister shop SSCG will continue to handle media duties for Amgen brands marketed to healthcare professionals.

title: Eduardo Escasany: "En la medida que baje la inflación, la gente ahorrará más en pesos"
summary: Eduardo Escasany, president of Grupo Financiero Galicia, predicts that as inflation decreases, Argentinians will save more in pesos, fueling a boom in credit. He highlights the solidity of the financial system and the potential for significant growth in mortgage loans, while also raising concerns about government financing in the local market potentially crowding out private sector credit. Escasany emphasizes the importance of tackling the informal economy and the slow but necessary process of building trust in the local currency.

title: 7 ETFs with Salesforce Exposure are Up
summary: Salesforce.com's $6.5 billion acquisition of MuleSoft sparked debate, with the stock trading lower despite the strategic importance of the deal. The article identifies seven ETFs with Salesforce exposure that saw gains shortly after the acquisition announcement, highlighting their performance and Salesforce's expansion goals. Salesforce aims to leverage MuleSoft to enhance customer connectivity across various cloud and data sources, with a long-term revenue target of $60 billion by 2034.

title: Universal Technical Institute to Launch Free Summer Program for High School Juniors Interested in the Transportation Industry
summary: Universal Technical Institute (UTI) is launching a free three-week "Ignite" summer program for high school juniors at 12 campuses nationwide, including Long Beach. The program offers hands-on training in automotive technician skills to introduce students to the transportation industry and potential career opportunities. This initiative aims to address the significant demand for trained technicians in the automotive, diesel, and collision repair industries.

title: La acción de Televisa cierra en peor nivel desde junio 2012
summary: Las acciones de Televisa cayeron a su nivel más bajo desde junio de 2012, cerrando en 54.05 pesos, tras una demanda colectiva en Estados Unidos. Mientras tanto, la Bolsa Mexicana de Valores avanzó 0.95%, impulsada por las ganancias de Alfa y su subsidiaria Alpek, que anunció la compra de una planta en EE.UU. Wall Street, por su parte, experimentó descensos tras el anuncio de la Reserva Federal de un aumento en la tasa de interés.

title: While nursing homes struggle financially, Genesis Healthcare is managing the turbulence
summary: Genesis Healthcare Inc. has undergone a major financial restructuring to navigate the turbulence in the nursing home industry, which is grappling with rising wages, stagnant Medicaid payment rates, and declining occupancy. Despite a significant loss in 2017, the company, with the help of landlords Welltower Inc. and Sabra Healthcare REIT Inc. cutting rents, is managing to stay afloat while other operators struggle or exit the business. CEO George V. Hager Jr. expresses optimism for the future, highlighting potential benefits from a projected decrease in nursing home bed supply and an eventual increase in demand from aging baby boomers.

title: The 1 Big Reason Dominion Energy Is a Better Value Stock than Duke Energy
summary: This article analyzes why Dominion Energy is considered a better value stock than Duke Energy for income investors, despite both being large U.S. utilities. While both offer similar yields and operations, Dominion's lower valuation and significantly higher projected dividend growth (up to 10% annually) make it a more compelling investment. The article highlights Dominion's strategic use of a limited partnership and the completion of major projects as drivers for its superior dividend growth potential.

title: Houston industrial services co. sees double-digit stock surge after earnings release
summary: DXP Enterprises Inc. experienced a significant stock surge following its recent earnings release, with earnings per share wildly surpassing analyst expectations by approximately 80 percent. This positive financial performance led to a double-digit increase in the company's stock value.

title: Privet Fund Management Says It Delivered Letter To The Issuer's Chairman, Peter Bassi, And Potbelly Corp​'s Board
summary: Privet Fund Management LLC announced that it delivered a letter to Peter Bassi, Chairman of Potbelly Corp, and the company's board on March 21, 2018. The fund further urged Potbelly Corp not to pursue entrenching tactics like unilaterally adding directors to its board.

title: Tractor maker Deere & Co fears a hit from Trump tariffs and retaliation
summary: Deere & Co CEO Samuel Allen expressed concerns about the financial impact of U.S. tariffs on steel imports, which could raise steel prices by 30 percent. He also feared retaliatory tariffs on American agricultural exports, warning of a potential global trade war that could remove U.S. farmers from the world market for corn and soybeans. Despite the challenges, Allen stated that Deere would absorb higher steel costs and aggressively work to cut other expenses to offset the impact.

title: Sherwin-Williams Celebrates New Waco, Texas Distribution Service Center Opening
summary: The Sherwin-Williams Company celebrated the grand opening of its new $39 million Distribution Service Center in Waco, Texas, a key transportation hub for paint distribution across eight states. This state-of-the-art facility highlights Sherwin-Williams' long-term commitment and partnership with the Waco community, supporting 326 associates and featuring significant sustainability initiatives. The center delivers 3 million pounds of paint product daily to 700 S-W paint stores and incorporates green practices like carbon footprint reduction and extensive recycling.

title: Agricultural manufacturer to open in Bryan County
summary: AGCO Corporation, an agricultural machinery manufacturer, will open a 75,000-square-foot assembly center in Bryan County, representing an investment of over $8 million and creating 31 jobs within three years. This new Savannah Assembly Center will be responsible for the final assembly and distribution of Massey Ferguson compact and utility tractors for the southeast market. This expansion is supported by the Development Authority of Bryan County and the Georgia Department of Economic Development, highlighting Bryan County's manufacturing resources and skilled workforce.

title: ATI Forged Products announces $95 million expansion of Cudahy plant: 125 new jobs planned
summary: Allegheny Technologies Inc. (ATI) announced a $95 million expansion at its Cudahy plant, creating 125 new jobs over the next two years. The expansion is supported by up to $7 million in tax credits from the Wisconsin Economic Development Corp. and will fund a new iso-thermal press and heat-treating capacity to meet aerospace industry demand. CEO Rich Harshman cited the growing aerospace market, particularly the jet-engine industry, as the reason for the investment, stating it is "life-sustaining" for the company.

title: Latin America best managed banks 2018: Chile
summary: Euromoney highlights Banco Santander-Chile as one of the best-managed banks in Latin America for 2018. The article discusses Chile's mature yet evolving financial system, noting that while products and regulation haven't been particularly sophisticated, changes are underway. The adoption of Basel III requirements, driven by a new banking law, is increasing regulatory scrutiny from analysts and is estimated to require an additional $2.7 billion for the system.

title: This Sustainable, Trump-Tariff-Hiked Budweiser’s for You
summary: Anheuser-Busch InBev is shifting its Budweiser brand to 100% renewable energy and will mark cans accordingly, aiming to boost sales in the U.S. Amid this sustainability effort, the company faces potential price increases for consumers due to President Trump’s 10% tariff on aluminum imports. CEO Carlos Brito anticipates a 2-3% price hike on Budweiser, which relies heavily on aluminum packaging, while also announcing global renewable energy goals by 2025.

title: Despite foreclosure moratorium, Blackstone-owned firm advances some foreclosures in Puerto Rico
summary: Despite a foreclosure moratorium issued by the FHA until May 2018, Blackstone-owned Finance of America has been actively pursuing foreclosures and related legal actions in Puerto Rico following Hurricane Maria. This firm, which specializes in reverse mortgages, has been criticized for its aggressive tactics and for advancing cases even when homeowners were displaced by the hurricane. Community groups have repeatedly requested Blackstone to support a yearlong moratorium and help homeowners, but these requests have largely gone unanswered.

title: Veteran Fidelity PM to retire, leaving $36bn in fund assets
summary: Matthew Conti, a veteran portfolio manager at Fidelity Investments, is set to retire at the end of December. Conti currently manages five mutual funds with nearly $36 billion in total assets, including the $31.6 billion Fidelity Total Bond fund. Following his departure, Michael Weaver will co-manage several of these funds starting April 2.

title: Chase rarely lends to people of color in DC – and it’s probably legal
summary: JPMorgan Chase & Co. rarely lends to people of color in the Washington D.C. area, a practice that appears to be legal due to the bank's lack of traditional deposit-taking branches in the district. This allows Chase to circumvent the Community Reinvestment Act, which mandates lending in low- and moderate-income areas. An analysis by Reveal shows significant disparities in loan denials for people of color compared to white applicants, even when income and loan size are similar.
source: Reveal from The Center for Investigative Reporting

title: PRESS RELEASE: T. Rowe Price: "Adulting" Is Harder Without Any Financial Education
summary: T. Rowe Price's tenth annual Parents, Kids & Money Survey reveals that financial education in school positively impacts young adults' financial behaviors, with those receiving it being more likely to budget, have emergency funds, and save for retirement. However, the study also highlights shortcomings, as many young adults still feel unprepared despite financial education, often due to late instruction and a narrow curriculum that frequently omits long-term goals like retirement planning. The survey suggests that while financial education is effective, there's a need for earlier, broader, and more consistent money conversations both in schools and at home to better prepare young adults for financial responsibilities.

title: This Austrian Activist Took on Facebook in Europe. He’s Ready to Do It Again
summary: Max Schrems, an Austrian lawyer, is preparing to file a barrage of lawsuits against companies under Europe's new General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR), which comes into effect on May 25th. Having previously won a case against Facebook that led to stricter data transfer rules, Schrems has founded an organization called noyb and secured significant crowdfunding to target companies that exploit personal data. He plans to focus on high-impact cases to enforce consumer data protection.

title: FedEx Express Ignites Students’ Motivation for Their Future Through One-Day Job Shadow Program
summary: FedEx Express hosted 15 high school students from Seitoku University Girls High School for a one-day job shadow program at its Makuhari office in Chiba. Students shadowed employees in various departments and gained insights into how their studies relate to real-world work. This initiative, part of FedEx's long-standing partnership with Junior Achievement Japan, aims to inspire students in their future career planning.

title: How Olin Stock Has Fared in 2018 Year-to-Date
summary: Olin (OLN) stock has underperformed the market in 2018, falling 15.5% year-to-date until March 19, 2018, primarily due to lower-than-expected 4Q17 earnings and anticipated maintenance in 1Q18. The stock's high beta and prevailing market volatility also contributed to its decline, with a 14-day RSI suggesting it's nearing oversold territory. Bearish sentiment is increasing, indicated by short interest data, reflecting negative investor outlook.

title: ATI expands operations at Cudahy facility, move expected to create 125 new jobs
summary: Allegheny Technologies Incorporated (ATI) is expanding its operations in Cudahy with a $95 million project. This expansion is expected to create approximately 125 new jobs to meet the growing demand in the aerospace jet engine market. The Wisconsin Economic Development Corporation (WEDC) is supporting this initiative with up to $7 million in state income tax credits.

title: Technical Analysis of Nuveen California Municipal Value Fund (NYSE:NCA)
summary: This article provides a technical analysis overview for Nuveen California Municipal Value Fund (NCA) based on various indicators. The analysis presents a neutral signal for the stock based on the combination of these technical indicators.

title: First Freight Futures ETF Focuses on Dry Bulk Shipping
summary: The first freight futures-backed ETF, the Breakwave Dry Bulk Shipping ETF (BDRY), has launched, offering investors direct exposure to changes in global trade. Managed by Breakwave Advisors and ETF Managers Group, this actively managed ETF tracks dry bulk freight futures to measure rates for shipping dry bulk. It allocates to Capesize, Panamax, and Supramax contracts, with an initial allocation of 50%, 40%, and 10% respectively.

title: Investing in Big India ETFs With Positive Outlook
summary: The article discusses the positive outlook for investing in large India-focused ETFs, specifically mentioning the iShares India 50 ETF (INDY) and the iShares MSCI India ETF (INDA). It highlights India's recent efforts to liberalize its financial markets and reduce government subsidies under Prime Minister Narendra Modi, making it an attractive emerging market for investors. The article also provides details on INDA's holdings and sector allocation.

title: After raising $756M in its IPO, Dropbox sees shares jump 36% in market debut
summary: Dropbox Inc. saw its shares jump 36% in its market debut after raising $756 million in its IPO, pricing shares at $21, higher than initial estimates. The company's valuation swelled to over $11 billion, marking the largest tech IPO since Snap Inc. last year. Despite not yet being profitable, the IPO's success is attributed to a Salesforce investment and a relatively small percentage of shares offered, creating scarcity.

title: FedEx Sinks Most in Five Years as Trump Tariffs Stoke Trade Fear
summary: FedEx Corp. shares experienced their largest drop in five years following President Donald Trump's order to impose tariffs on Chinese imports, sparking fears of reduced global trade. The company, which operates the world's largest cargo airline and has a significant presence in Asia and China due to its acquisition of Tiger International Inc., is considered particularly vulnerable to trade slowdowns. An analyst noted that FedEx will "feel it" if China shipments decline due to tariffs.

title: Cemex se desiste de aumentar capital como había planeado
summary: Cemex announced it will no longer seek a capital increase of up to 3,750 million titles after discussions with shareholders. Instead, the company will limit its proposal to emit a maximum of 1% of its outstanding shares. This decision comes as Cemex aims to regain its investment grade and will be discussed at an extraordinary general shareholders' meeting on April 5th.

title: Gaia Announces Pricing of Public Offering of Class A Common Stock
summary: Gaia, Inc. announced the pricing of its underwritten registered public offering of 2,333,333 shares of Class A common stock at $15 per share, with an option for underwriters to purchase an additional 350,000 shares. The offering is expected to generate approximately $35 million in gross proceeds, with net proceeds of about $32.3 million designated for general corporate purposes, including working capital. B. Riley FBR, Inc. is the sole book-running manager for the offering.

title: STG Stock Price and Chart — NYSE:STG
summary: This page provides an overview of Sunlands Technology Group (NYSE:STG) stock, including its current price, historical performance, key financial metrics, and company information. It also features a collection of trading ideas and technical analysis summaries from various contributors. The company, founded in 2003 and headquartered in Beijing, China, specializes in online post-secondary and professional education.

title: AbbVie | $ABBV Stock | Shares Fall 11% After A Disappointing Cancer Drug Experiment
summary: Shares of AbbVie, Inc. ($ABBV) fell over 11% after the pharmaceutical company announced a setback in an experiment for its cancer drug, rovalpituzumab tesirine, leading them to withdraw their fast approval request from the FDA. This marked the worst single-day drop for the stock since its IPO six years prior. Despite this, AbbVie had previously boosted its 2018 earnings forecast and projects higher revenue due to its diverse drug portfolio, successful products like HUMIRA, and favorable tax laws.

title: Dropbox’s IPO Debuts at $29 a Share
summary: Dropbox's IPO debuted at $29 a share, opening with a strong performance that saw its stock surge by as much as 44% on its first trading day, valuing the company at nearly $12 billion. The cloud-storage company priced its IPO at $21 a share and has a dual-class stock structure, with co-founder and CEO Andrew Houston owning 24% and Sequoia Capital holding a 25% stake. Despite a significant reduction in net loss to $111.7 million and positive free-cash flow, the company warned investors that it may never be profitable and highlighted risks like data and security breaches.

title: Class Actions vs Individual lawsuits: The Equifax Litigation
summary: This article discusses the various legal actions taken against Equifax following its 2017 data breach, contrasting class actions with individual lawsuits in both Canada and the United States. It details specific class action developments in British Columbia and Ontario, highlighting the legal considerations and complexities involved, such as carriage motions and the scope of claims. The article also touches upon the use of small claims courts by some American victims and the inherent drawbacks of that approach.

title: Report: Kroger, Target flirt with mega-merger
summary: Kroger and Target are reportedly discussing a possible mega-merger, with talks ongoing since last summer. The potential deal, valued at over $35 billion, would create a $195 billion sales entity with 4,600 stores nationwide, aiming to better compete against Walmart and Amazon. While Wall Street's reaction was muted, some analysts express skepticism that such a combination would resolve underlying e-commerce weaknesses for either company.

title: Wynn shareholder reshuffle not to hurt Macau market: DICJ
summary: Macau’s casino regulator, the Gaming Inspection and Coordination Bureau (DICJ), stated that the recent shareholder reshuffle at Wynn Resorts Ltd, which includes Galaxy Entertainment Group Ltd acquiring a 4.9-percent stake, will not negatively impact Macau’s gaming sector. The regulator affirmed its commitment to monitoring the situation to ensure sustainable development. Analysts from Sanford C.Bernstein noted that this acquisition could lead to collaboration between Wynn Resorts and Galaxy Entertainment on future development opportunities, especially in Japan.

title: Macau | Foothold deal at Wynn Resorts by Galaxy could lead to purchase of Wynn Macau - Analysts
summary: Analysts from Sanford C. Bernstein believe Galaxy Entertainment Group's (GEG) purchase of a nearly 5% stake in Wynn Resorts could eventually lead to GEG acquiring Wynn Macau, creating a dominant Macau gaming company. The deal, valued at US$927.5 million, is seen as beneficial for both parties, potentially allowing Wynn Resorts to repay a significant bridging loan and opening opportunities for future joint ventures in Asia, such as a possible integrated resort in Japan. The sale also notes Steve Wynn's full divestment of his shares, which is expected to reduce regulatory scrutiny on Wynn Resorts.

title: Target, Kroger shares rise on merger report, but source tells CNBC there are no talks
summary: Shares of Target and Kroger experienced a surge in premarket trading following a Fast Company report about potential merger discussions. However, sources close to the matter informed CNBC that no merger talks are occurring; instead, the companies have met regarding a Shipt partnership. Despite the denial, the initial report caused significant stock price movements, highlighting market interest in potential collaborations in the competitive retail and grocery sectors.

title: U.S. retirement plans abandoning active funds for investment trusts
summary: U.S. retirement plans are increasingly shifting away from costly actively managed funds towards collective investment trusts (CITs) to save money. This trend is driven by CITs mimicking popular mutual funds with similar returns but at a lower cost, leading to billions of dollars flowing out of active funds and into CITs at major firms like T. Rowe Price and Fidelity. Industry projections suggest that assets in CITs could exceed $3 trillion this year, indicating a significant and ongoing shift in retirement investment strategies.

title: Wells Fargo says four top risk management executives to retire: WSJ
summary: Wells Fargo's top four risk management executives are retiring as the bank nears a regulatory settlement, following an enforcement action by the Federal Reserve and anticipated action from the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency. These retirements are part of a reorganization aimed at strengthening the bank's risk management functions in the wake of widespread scandals. The departing executives include Jim Richards, Kevin Oden, Keb Byers, and Vic Albrecht, all discussed with regulators.

title: Wayne Huizenga, who built his fortune from Blockbuster, waste management, dies at 80
summary: H. Wayne Huizenga, the entrepreneur who built business empires including Blockbuster Entertainment, AutoNation, and Waste Management Inc., has died at the age of 80. He also owned three professional sports franchises: the Florida Marlins, Florida Panthers, and Miami Dolphins, achieving a World Series win with the Marlins but never a Super Bowl with the Dolphins. Huizenga was known for his ability to build companies rapidly and for his impact on both business and sports in South Florida.

title: Bank of America pays $42 million fine in New York 'masking' probe
summary: Bank of America Corp (BAC) will pay a $42 million fine and admitted wrongdoing to settle claims by New York's attorney general that it fraudulently routed clients' stock trades to outside firms, including one run by swindler Bernard Madoff. The bank was accused of "masking" schemes that affected over 16 million trade orders and 4 billion shares, making its electronic trading services appear safer and more sophisticated than they were. This fine marks the largest collected by New York State to resolve an electronic trading probe.

The reports highlight strong business performance, including profit improvement and dividend prioritization, and emphasize the company's commitment to sustainable progress through remanufacturing, innovative customer support, and community involvement via the Caterpillar Foundation. Caterpillar's strategy focuses on long-term profitable growth, operational excellence, and providing solutions that make safe, productive, and efficient use of resources.

title: 7 Small-Cap ETFs to Help You Win a Trade War
summary: This article suggests a strategy for investors to mitigate risks during a potential trade war by focusing on small-cap exchange-traded funds (ETFs) that invest in companies less connected to global commerce. It highlights seven specific small-cap ETFs, detailing their investment focus, key holdings, and how they might offer insulation from protectionist policies. The ETFs range from broad market small-cap funds to those focusing on growth, value, micro-cap, dividend payers, gold miners, and consumer discretionary sectors.

title: New Sprouts Farmers Market location seeking more than 140 employees
summary: Sprouts Farmers Market is opening a new 30,000-square-foot store in Las Vegas, its sixth location in the city, on August 1st. The new store will create approximately 140 full and part-time job opportunities, including various department roles, cashiers, and administrative positions. Sprouts is seeking team members who are passionate about healthy eating and organic products.

title: An old Wall Street money manager with $500 billion is moving to Nashville from Manhattan to save money
summary: Asset manager AllianceBernstein, with $549 billion in assets under management, is moving its headquarters from Midtown Manhattan to Nashville, Tennessee, relocating approximately 1,050 jobs to save money on operating costs, living expenses, and taxes. The company plans to invest over $70 million in the city, with the transition expected to be completed by 2022, while finance-related operations will remain in New York. The move is driven by lower living expenses and taxes in Tennessee compared to New York, and aligns with AllianceBernstein's strategy to achieve ongoing expense savings despite transitional costs.

title: Kent Avenue welcomes Dime Community Bank during grand opening ceremony
summary: Dime Community Bank celebrated the grand opening of its newest branch at 149 Kent Avenue in Williamsburg. This new location marks a return to the bank's original roots, having started on Kent Avenue in 1864. The branch features a customer-friendly design, universal bankers for streamlined service, and has already been actively engaging with the local community through donations and outreach.

title: Railroads offering up to $25,000 for new hires
summary: Railroads are offering significant signing bonuses, up to $25,000, to attract new hires amid a challenging employment market. Companies like Union Pacific Corp. and BNSF Railway are providing these incentives, even for positions that do not require prior experience. However, these bonuses often come with conditions, such as required tenure at a specific location, and the jobs themselves can be demanding, with some requiring 24/7 availability.

title: US warehouse club chain, PriceSmart, eyes Guyana due to “future prosperity”
summary: US-headquartered warehouse club, PriceSmart, is planning to establish operations in Guyana, citing the country's expected economic boom from oil production. PriceSmart's founder, Robert Price, and other board members met with Guyanese Minister of State, Joseph Harmon, to explore investment opportunities, with Harmon assuring government support for the venture. PriceSmart currently operates 40 membership warehouse clubs across 12 countries and one US territory.

title: Tariff Impact Colors a Key House Race in Boeing Country (Published 2018)
summary: The article discusses the impact of President Trump's trade policies, particularly tariffs, on a key House race in Washington State, a region heavily reliant on trade with China due to Boeing's presence. Boeing workers and business owners expressed concern about potential trade wars affecting their livelihoods and jobs. The congressional race in "Boeing Country" serves as a crucial test of how Trump's trade policies might affect Republican candidates.

title: E-commerce delivery demand lifts XPO first-quarter profit, but costs rise
summary: XPO Logistics reported a rise in first-quarter profit driven by strong e-commerce delivery demand, though the company faced increased costs due to wage hikes and investments in technology and new hubs. Despite higher expenses, XPO exceeded analyst expectations for earnings per share and plans to pursue one or two acquisitions by year-end to continue its growth strategy.

title: Not all Roads Lead to the Kentucky Derby (Published 2018)
summary: Churchill Downs' efforts to attract international horses to the Kentucky Derby have faced significant challenges, including injuries and high travel costs, despite optimism from officials. Both the European and Japan Roads to the Kentucky Derby have struggled to consistently bring competitive international entries. Despite these setbacks, Churchill Downs remains committed to growing the Derby brand internationally and continuing its efforts to attract global participants.

title: A Busy First Quarter For Enphase Energy
summary: Enphase Energy reported a busy first quarter with revenues of $70.0 million, a 28% increase year-over-year, and a GAAP gross margin of 26.2%. The company continued its progress toward its 30-20-10 operating model, expanded its AC module partnerships, and shipped 611,000 microinverters globally. Enphase also received the Dutch Solar Innovation Award 2018 for its seventh-generation microinverters.

title: Backlash-Struck E-Mart to Return to China Via Partner
summary: South Korean retailer E-Mart is returning to the China market through a partnership with Dutch firm Spar International, supplying goods like cookies and teas. This move follows E-Mart's withdrawal from most of its China stores due to weak sales and consumer backlash linked to Sino-South Korean tensions over the THAAD missile system deployment. E-Mart's sales in China declined 30% to 113 billion won ($105 million) last year.

title: Four miners die after being trapped in Sibanye-Stillwater mine
summary: Four miners have died after being trapped underground at Sibanye-Stillwater's Masakhane mine following a 2.2 magnitude earthquake which caused a cave-in. While 10 of the 13 trapped employees were rescued, four succumbed to their injuries, and two remain unaccounted for. This incident follows a previous event in February where over 1,000 mineworkers were rescued after being trapped at another Sibanye-Stillwater mine due to a power outage.

title: Want a $25,000 bonus? These railroad companies are desperate for help
summary: BNSF Railway and Union Pacific Corp. are offering sign-on bonuses of up to $25,000 to attract new workers amidst a tight labor market. These incentives are for mechanical workers, mechanics, electricians, and railcar repair workers across several states, with bonuses paid out over a three-year period contingent on continued employment.

title: Entergy Mississippi Celebrates 95 Years with 2 Mississippi Museums Gift
summary: Entergy Mississippi is celebrating its 95th anniversary by donating $25,000 to the Mississippi Civil Rights Museum and the Museum of Mississippi History. This donation will cover free admission for the first 95 visitors to the museums every day in May. The company previously contributed $1 million towards the establishment of these museums.

title: Agnico focuses on expanding in Nunavut
summary: Agnico Eagle Mines Ltd. is expanding its operations in Nunavut with the Amaruq and Meliadine gold mine development projects, aiming to boost annual gold production to 2 million ounces by 2020. The Meadowbank Mine, nearing the end of its reserves, will transition to processing ore from Amaruq, while the Meliadine project is ahead of schedule for production in mid-2019. These new mines are expected to significantly contribute to Agnico's gold output.

title: Avis Budget Group | $CAR Stock | Shares Sink Following Q1 Earnings
summary: Avis Budget Group (NYSE: CAR) shares dropped 11% despite beating Q1 earnings and revenue estimates, with the company reaffirming its full-year guidance. The company reported a net loss of $0.74 per share but revenue increased by 7% to $1.97 billion, driven by higher rental days and currency exchange benefits. CEO Larry De Shon noted a positive start to fiscal year 2018 with improved utilization, strong demand, and stabilized pricing and fleet costs in the Americas.

title: Caterpillar taps Andrew Bonfield for CFO post
summary: Caterpillar Inc. has appointed Andrew Bonfield as its new chief financial officer, following the retirement of Brad Halverson. Bonfield previously served as a CFO for National Grid plc, Cadbury, and Bristol-Myers Squibb, bringing extensive global financial experience. He will assume the role on September 1, with Joe Creed serving as interim CFO until then.

title: Mid Continent Cabinetry to close Cottonwood plant
summary: Norcraft Companies, parent company of Mid Continent Cabinetry, announced it would close its Cottonwood plant later this year, affecting 200 employees. The company cited changes in market conditions and consumer tastes as reasons for the closure, with manufacturing moving to other Norcraft locations. Efforts will be made to assist affected employees with compensation, resources, and job placement assistance.

title: Charles Schwab picks Austin, San Francisco for digital hubs to fix 'mundane' aspects of banking
summary: Charles Schwab is establishing new "digital accelerator" teams in Austin and San Francisco to enhance technological tools for both retail banking and institutional customers. These hubs will employ hundreds of existing and new staff to develop innovative solutions aimed at improving efficiency in banking operations. The initiative focuses on addressing typical banking tasks to streamline processes through digital advancements.

title: American Airlines Dropping Two Regional Carriers
summary: American Airlines will not renew contracts with regional carriers ExpressJet and Trans State when they expire in 2019, aiming to streamline the passenger experience. SkyWest Airlines is expected to take over ExpressJet's routes, while Envoy Airlines will reportedly handle Trans State's routes. This move follows American Airlines' earlier termination of a contract with Air Wisconsin Airlines in February.

title: Trading Giant Virtu Financial Will Make Markets in ‘Physical Bitcoin’ Once It’s More Regulated
summary: High-frequency trading firm Virtu Financial plans to enter the cryptocurrency spot markets as a major market maker once the asset class becomes more regulated. CEO Douglas Cifu explained that while Virtu currently acts as a market maker in bitcoin futures, the company has concerns about the lack of regulation and centralized clearing in "cash bitcoin" markets. However, the firm is prepared to engage directly in spot crypto trading once the industry matures with better regulatory frameworks and clearing mechanisms.

summary: The city of Richmond and Chevron Corp. have agreed to a $5 million settlement in a lawsuit stemming from a 2012 refinery fire that caused a large plume of smoke and resulted in 15,000 people seeking medical treatment. The agreement concludes the city's 2013 lawsuit, with funds to be used for public safety, education, parks, recreation, and community development. Both parties acknowledge Chevron's efforts to enhance refinery safety and cleaner operations.

title: Berkshire Hathaway Has Exited IBM: Buffett
summary: Warren Buffett announced that Berkshire Hathaway has completely sold off its stake in IBM, a position once valued at $10.7 billion. This decision followed IBM's continued underperformance, with Berkshire previously having dumped 94.5% of its shares by the end of 2017. Concurrently, Buffett reallocated funds into Apple, significantly increasing Berkshire's holdings in the smartphone maker.

title: Why Lululemon Athletica Stock Gained 12% in April
summary: Lululemon Athletica (LULU) stock gained 12% in April, outperforming the S&P 500, due to strong first-quarter operating results and positive investor sentiment. The company reported a 12% increase in online sales and a 2 percentage point rise in gross profit margin, leading to an 80% stock rally over the past year. Lululemon expects continued sales growth and increased earnings per share for 2018, despite a leadership transition.

title: Wells Fargo agrees to pay $480 million to settle securities-fraud lawsuit over fake accounts
summary: Wells Fargo & Co. has agreed to pay $480 million to settle a class-action lawsuit alleging securities fraud tied to its fake-accounts scandal. The bank, while denying allegations, opted for the settlement to avoid further litigation and stated it had already set aside reserves. This settlement is part of a series of financial penalties and actions taken against Wells Fargo for its past misconduct, including a recent $1 billion penalty for mortgage and auto-loan abuses.

title: In Comanche, sicknesses stop cleanup work at a former refinery
summary: Cleanup work at a former Phillips 66 refinery in Comanche, Oklahoma, has been temporarily halted due to residents experiencing illnesses blamed on an overpowering odor emanating from the site. Residents report symptoms like troubled breathing, headaches, nausea, and stomach pains. Phillips 66 has paused operations out of an abundance of caution and is collecting air quality data, while the Oklahoma Department of Environmental Quality oversees the situation.

title: Ramon Ang: SMC has deep pockets to build ‘aerotropolis’ on its own
summary: Ramon Ang, president and CEO of San Miguel Corp. (SMC), stated the company has the financial capability to independently build the P735.6-billion Bulacan International Airport Project, despite interest from other firms to partner. The Department of Finance initially had reservations about the project being handled by a subsidiary, but clarified that partnerships are allowed and emphasized the need for SMC to demonstrate financial and technical capability. The project, approved by the Neda board, still needs to undergo negotiations and a Swiss challenge before final terms are set.

This comes as the company navigates investment for growth, integration, and maintaining a substantial dividend yielding over 11%. Despite criticism from the Communications Workers of America, CenturyLink emphasized its commitment to long-term profitable revenue growth and free cash flow generation to sustain its dividend, with CEO transition from Glen Post to Jeff Storey imminent.

title: Marathon-Andeavor merge
summary: Marathon Petroleum is set to acquire Andeavor for $23.3 billion, creating the largest independent fuel maker in the United States. This merger will impact key refining and export facilities in Alaska, particularly the Kenai refinery and LNG facility. The deal aims to leverage export port access and capitalize on increasing fuel demand and the tight oil boom, with the combined company being well-positioned for upcoming regulations to reduce shipping pollution.

summary: Deere and Hitachi invited two prominent contracting firms, CK Contractors & Development and Hoopaugh Grading Company, to their Kernersville, N.C., factory for a roundtable discussion. The event celebrated 30 years of the John Deere Hitachi factory and its recent $150 million expansion, focusing on equipment quality, reliability, service from James River Equipment, and the impact of technology like grade control on their operations. Contractors highlighted the critical role of dealership support in minimizing downtime and maximizing productivity.

summary: Indonesia's markets and country-specific ETFs have significantly underperformed in the emerging markets category due to foreign investors withdrawing capital. ETFs like iShares MSCI Indonesia ETF (EIDO) and Market Vectors Indonesia Index ETF (IDX) saw substantial declines, with the rupiah also depreciating. This sell-off highlights the vulnerability of Indonesia's local-currency debt market to global changes, particularly given the high foreign ownership of government bonds.

title: Essent still sees a Bermuda tax advantage
summary: Essent Group Ltd executives affirmed that the company's Bermuda structure still provides a tax advantage, despite recent US tax reforms. The mortgage insurer and reinsurer reported strong first-quarter profits, beating analyst expectations, and noted that its Bermuda-based reinsurer, Essent Re, contributes to a lower effective tax rate of approximately 16.5 percent compared to the 21 percent US corporate rate. This structure allows Essent to achieve higher returns while maintaining a competitive pricing strategy.

title: Medtronic Hires JPMorgan Analyst, and Investors Rate It a ‘Buy’
summary: Medtronic Plc has hired former JPMorgan Chase & Co. analyst Mike Weinstein as its new senior vice president of strategy, a move that has been met positively by investors, causing the company’s shares to rise. Weinstein, who covered Medtronic for two decades at JPMorgan, will focus on deals and boosting the share price.

title: Nestle Takes Over Sales of Starbucks in Grocery Aisles
summary: Nestle is paying over $7 billion to take over the global retail sales of Starbucks's coffee and tea products outside of its cafes, a move expected to significantly boost Nestle's market presence in the U.S. This deal includes rights to market and distribute various Starbucks packaged coffee and tea brands and allows Nestle to use the Starbucks brand on its single-serve capsules. Approximately 500 Starbucks employees will join Nestle, and operations will remain in Seattle, with the deal anticipating regulatory approval and closure by year-end.

title: Canada Faces ‘Critical Competitiveness Challenge,’ RBC CEO Says
summary: David McKay, CEO of Royal Bank of Canada, warns that Canada faces a critical competitiveness challenge and must act with "tremendous urgency" to avoid being left behind by countries like the U.S. and China. He advocates for improved training and investment in infrastructure, while also expressing confidence in a forthcoming Nafta deal.

title: Why Philip Morris International Inc. Stock Lost 17.5% in April
summary: Philip Morris International Inc. stock dropped 17.5% in April following mixed first-quarter earnings results, primarily due to a significant decline in sales of its iQOS heated-tobacco electronic cigarettes from the previous quarter. Despite overall year-over-year sales growth, the softness in this key product line, crucial for long-term growth as the company pivots away from traditional cigarettes, caused a steep sell-off. title: Global Insurer Argo Group Switches Exchange Listing to NYSE
summary: Argo Group International Holdings, a specialty insurance underwriter, has moved its stock listing from NASDAQ to the New York Stock Exchange (NYSE) to reach a broader base of global investors and enhance shareholder value. Coinciding with the move, the company reported a positive first quarter driven by increased gross written premiums and net investment income, despite significant claims losses in 2017. Argo Group also declared a quarterly cash dividend of $0.27 per share and saw an initial positive jump in its stock price on the NYSE.

title: Call-center operator to lay off 77 workers, but offer other positions
summary: Concentrix Services US Inc., a call center and technical support operator in Milwaukee, announced it will lay off 77 employees, primarily at its northwest side location. The layoffs are due to a client determining fewer people were needed for engagement services. However, the company plans to offer other positions, including work-from-home options, to many of the affected employees who are in good standing.

title: Shell to Exit Canadian Natural Resources for $3.3 Billion
summary: Royal Dutch Shell Plc announced its agreement to sell all its shares in Canadian Natural Resources Ltd. for $3.3 billion. This divestment aims to shed a less environmentally friendly asset and reduce the debt incurred from its $50 billion acquisition of BG Group Plc.

title: International Association of Women Honors Beatrice Felix as a 2018-2019 Influencer of the Year
summary: The International Association of Women (IAW) honored Beatrice Felix as a 2018-2019 Influencer of the Year for her outstanding leadership in entrepreneurship. As a Consultant at Heartland Institute of Financial Education, Ms. Felix promotes financial literacy and assists high school students with college preparation. She is also the founder of Pivotal Mind Coaching, where she helps individuals achieve their professional and personal goals.

title: Why there's millions to be made in moving oil from Permian Basin to Houston
summary: Oil producers in the Permian Basin face a significant price discount for their crude compared to Houston due to pipeline capacity constraints and heavy rail traffic for fracking sand. This creates a potential arbitrage opportunity for traders to earn about $8 a barrel by shipping oil via rail, despite the logistical challenges and competition for rail resources with fracking sand. The situation has led to "haves and have-nots" among Permian producers based on their transportation arrangements.

title: Global X's BOTZ ETF Named "ETF of the Year" at the Mutual Fund Industry Awards
summary: The Global X Robotics and Artificial Intelligence ETF (BOTZ) received multiple accolades at the Mutual Fund Industry Awards, including "ETF of the Year," "ETF Innovation of the Year," and "Thematic ETF of the Year." The fund, which started 2017 with nearly $5 million in AUM, grew to attract over $2.5 billion in net new assets by April 2018, recognized for its strong performance, flows, and innovative objective in the rapidly growing robotics and AI sectors. Global X emphasizes providing investors with efficient access to revolutionary industries through its thematic ETF strategies.

title: Shell to sell entire interest in Canadian Natural Resources for $4.3B
summary: Royal Dutch Shell is selling its entire stake of over 97 million shares in Calgary-based Canadian Natural Resources Ltd. for approximately $4.3 billion. This sale represents an approximate eight percent stake in CNRL, with proceeds intended to reduce Shell's net debt. The move follows Shell's previous sale of its Alberta oilsands assets to Canadian Natural for $11.1 billion in cash and stock, indicating a continued strategic shift away from oilsands operations towards higher-return assets.

title: Boeing will lose out on $20 billion in Iran deals as Airbus, GE impacted
summary: Boeing is set to lose approximately $20 billion in potential deals with Iran following the U.S. withdrawal from the 2015 nuclear agreement. This decision, which imposes sanctions on businesses dealing with Iran, will also impact Airbus SE and General Electric Co. Boeing had agreements to sell 110 planes to Iranian airlines, none of which had been delivered or logged in its order book.

summary: This infographic details the CME CF Bitcoin Reference Rate (BRR) and CME CF Bitcoin Real-Time Index (BRTI), highlighting their role in professionalizing bitcoin trading. title: Herc Holdings narrows losses in Q1, reports double- digit increase in revenue
summary: Herc Holdings narrowed its losses in the first quarter, reporting a loss of $10.1 million compared to $39.2 million a year ago, attributing the improvement to strategic initiatives. The company saw a double-digit increase in total revenue to $431.3 million, with equipment rental revenue up 15 percent. Herc also raised its financial outlook for the year, expecting adjusted earnings of $630 million to $660 million before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization.

title: Kimco Realty Helps Put Dania Beach on the Map
summary: Kimco Realty is transforming a former industrial area in Dania Beach, Florida, into Dania Pointe, a major mixed-use development. This project, which includes retail, restaurants, hotels, and residential units, is expected to elevate Dania Beach from a "pass-through" city to a "destination" location, boosting tourism, creating jobs, and generating significant tax revenue for the city and state. The development involved overcoming complex issues like diverse land ownership, creative zoning, and significant engineering challenges to revitalize the 102-acre site.

title: Monster Beverage’s sales and profit surge, but margin pressures haunt outlook
summary: Monster Beverage saw strong sales and profit growth in the first quarter of 2018, driven by international expansion and the Monster Energy brand. However, the company is facing concerns about future margin pressures due to higher input costs for aluminum, fuel, and freight, raising questions about its ability to pass these costs on to consumers. Analysts have expressed disappointment and are watching the situation closely given rising gas prices and their impact on convenience store shoppers.

title: Why Martin Marietta's CEO expects a 'record year'
summary: Martin Marietta Materials CEO Ward Nye anticipates a "record year" for the Raleigh aggregates firm, with North Carolina expected to be a key driver of its success. This outlook was shared with analysts, highlighting the company's strong performance projections.

summary: This article highlights the benefits of working with colleagues from diverse backgrounds, focusing on case studies from BD Singapore, KPMG Singapore, and Mundipharma. title: Short-sellers bring Singapore tech darling Venture down to earth
summary: Venture Corp, a Singaporean tech company, experienced a significant stock decline after a period of rapid growth due to a short-seller attack and disappointing sales from Philip Morris, a key client. Despite the market volatility caused by anonymous bloggers and analyst downgrades, the company's CEO and some investors remain confident, with Venture initiating share buybacks and seeing a slight recovery.

title: This Week’s ETF Launches: The First Bond ETF Focused on the S&P 500
summary: ProShares has launched the first bond ETF focused on the S&P 500, offering exposure to investment-grade bonds from the biggest companies in the index. Additionally, USCF introduced a new commodities fund designed to avoid the tax complexities of a K-1 form, making commodity investing more accessible. These new ETFs aim to provide investors with innovative ways to gain exposure to the bond and commodity markets.

title: CP Rail raising quarterly dividend by 15.5 per cent
summary: Canadian Pacific Railway Ltd. is increasing its quarterly dividend by 15.5 per cent, raising payments to 65 cents per share from 56.25 cents per share. The railway also bought back approximately 4.4 million of its shares in May at a weighted average price of $214.31, a move that enhances return on equity and earnings per share.

title: AXA Equitable Flops in Largest IPO of the Year
summary: AXA Equitable's initial public offering, the largest of the year, saw its shares debut at $20, significantly below the targeted range of $24 to $27. This weak reception indicates that recent strength in the new-issue market is primarily concentrated in the technology sector, with AXA Equitable's stock opening 1.7% higher than its pricing. According to Dealogic, only 10% of U.S.-listed IPOs since 2010 have priced so far below the midpoint of their targeted range.

title: Prominent Houston bank board member sells $3.7M in stock
summary: Ned Holmes, a board member of Prosperity Bank (NYSE: PB), sold approximately 50,000 shares of the company's stock on May 7 and 8. The shares were sold at roughly $74 each, totaling $3.7 million, according to an SEC filing. This transaction represents the largest Houston-based bank by market cap.

title: S&P 500 Sector Weightings; Tech Nears 26%
summary: The Technology sector now constitutes nearly 26% of the S&P 500, a weighting not seen since late 1999/early 2000. This makes it larger than the smallest six sectors combined. Other key sectors like Financials and Health Care follow, while Energy, Consumer Staples, and Industrials have seen their weightings decline to single digits.

title: After stunning victory, Malaysian leader Mahathir says he only ‘wants to restore the rule of law’
summary: Mahathir Mohamad, after a surprising victory in Malaysia's general election, stated his intention to restore the rule of law rather than seek revenge against former Prime Minister Najib Razak. His opposition alliance secured a simple majority, ending 60 years of rule by the Barisan Nasional coalition. Mahathir's administration plans to review foreign investments and reverse the goods and services tax, though his promises have raised concerns among credit rating agencies.

title: Nabors Announces Pricing Of Common Shares And Mandatory Convertible Preferred Shares
summary: Nabors Industries Ltd. announced the pricing of its offerings of 35,000,000 common shares at $7.75 per share and 5,000,000 mandatory convertible preferred shares at $50 per share. The gross proceeds are expected to be $521,250,000, which Nabors intends to use to repay borrowings under its revolving credit facility and for general corporate purposes. The offerings are anticipated to close around May 14, 2018, with Morgan Stanley and Citigroup acting as book-running managers.

title: US insurer Cigna sees China as biggest international market
summary: US health insurer Cigna expects China to become its largest international market due to its expanding middle class, aging population, and rise of chronic diseases. The company is deepening its operations in China through a joint venture with China Merchant Bank and is expanding into more provinces. While Cigna's international business has shown consistent double-digit growth, South Korea is currently its biggest overseas market.
