PowerPlan offers regulatory, tax, and budgeting strategies, and Roper anticipates it will generate $150 million in revenue and $60 million in after-tax cash flow in the first year. The acquisition is expected to conclude in the second quarter, pending regulatory approval, and analysts note Roper Technologies Inc. (NYSE:ROP) is currently priced with low risk.

title: Construction equipment rental market expected to exceed $140 billion by 2024
summary: The construction equipment rental market is projected to surpass $140 billion by 2024, driven by increasing residential and commercial construction worldwide. Large-scale government projects and the financial benefits of renting over owning heavy machinery are key contributors to this growth. Despite challenges like economic fluctuations and a shortage of skilled labor, the earthmoving and road building equipment segment will dominate, and the European market is expected to see significant growth as companies shift towards renting.

title: CBI Charges 17 Including Sify Employees In SSC Paper Leak Case
summary: The CBI has charged 17 persons, including 10 employees of Sify Technologies Pvt Ltd and seven students, in connection with the leak of a paper for the Staff Selection Commission graduate level examination. Searches were conducted at 12 locations, including Sify offices and the residence of an employee identified as Sant Prasad Gupta, who was the custodian of the question bank. The leak involved the Quantitative Ability paper for the Combined Graduate Level (Tier-II) Examination 2017, which surfaced on social media before the exam began.

title: Clorox Announces New $2 Billion Stock Repurchase Program
summary: The Clorox Company announced a new $2 billion stock repurchase program authorized by its board of directors. This program aims to return value to stockholders, replace an existing $750 million program, and demonstrates confidence in the company's 2020 Strategy and strong cash flow generation while maintaining a healthy debt-to-EBITDA ratio.

title: Netflix Stock Hits Record High, Briefly Making It More Valuable Than Disney
summary: Netflix's market capitalization briefly surpassed Disney's on Thursday after its stock rallied to a record high. While this milestone is symbolic given Netflix's smaller revenue compared to Disney and Comcast, it reflects strong investor confidence in its growth prospects. The company continues to invest heavily in original content, driving subscriber growth despite significant spending.

title: Whirlpool Corp. (WHR) Is Losing Ground In Early Trade
summary: Whirlpool Corp. (WHR) experienced a significant drop in early trading, falling 12.33 to $152.32 and reaching nearly a 3-week low. The stock gapped open lower on Thursday morning and continued to decline.

title: Con Edison’s $1.5B Investment and Technology Get Delivery Systems Ready for Summer
summary: Con Edison has invested $1.5 billion in its electric delivery systems and new technologies to prepare for the summer, including a 12-megawatt hour battery system in Queens. The company anticipates higher residential bills due to supply charges but is offering incentives for energy efficiency, solar adoption, and smart home devices. These efforts aim to ensure reliable service while helping customers reduce energy consumption and environmental impact.

title: Citron's Andrew Left discusses his short on Inogen shares
summary: Andrew Left, founder of Citron Research, discusses his short position on Inogen (INGN). Inogen is a California-based company that specializes in developing and manufacturing oxygen tanks. The discussion took place during CNBC's Halftime Report.

title: Netflix Briefly Tops Disney Market Value
summary: Netflix Inc. briefly surpassed Walt Disney Co. in market value on Thursday, making it the most valuable media company. Netflix shares rose 1.3 percent to $349.29, boosting its market cap to $151.8 billion, while Disney's declined 0.8 percent to $152.2 billion. This event highlights investor focus on subscriber growth for Netflix despite its significant cash burn.

title: Netflix briefly tops Disney as the biggest pure media company in the world by market value
summary: Netflix briefly surpassed Disney in market value, becoming the most valuable media company in the world. This marks a significant milestone given Netflix's strong stock performance, up nearly 82% this year, while Disney's stock is down about 5%. Wall Street analysts predict continued international subscriber growth for Netflix, despite Disney's efforts to compete in the streaming market.

title: Netflix overtakes Disney to become most valuable US media company
summary: Netflix surpassed Disney to become the most valuable US media company with a market capitalization of nearly $162bn, driven by its subscriber growth and a 70% stock increase since January. This shift is also influenced by Disney's potential acquisition challenges with 21st Century Fox and changing media consumption habits. The streaming giant has also secured content deals with high-profile figures like Barack and Michelle Obama, Shonda Rhimes, and Ryan Murphy, intensifying competition with other tech companies investing heavily in content.

title: Moody’s Sounds Junk Bond Alarm
summary: Moody's is issuing a warning about potential widespread junk bond defaults when the economy experiences its next downturn. This alert suggests concerns about the stability of the high-yield bond market in future economic contractions.

title: Spending Boom in China's Smaller Cities
summary: Consumption in China’s smaller cities is expected to triple between 2017 and 2030, driven by favorable government policies, population growth, higher household incomes, and increased willingness to spend. Morgan Stanley predicts these lower-tier cities will be the primary engine for China's overall private consumption market, with significant implications for consumer-focused industries and global investors. Key factors include a more flexible Hukou policy, improved infrastructure, and a stronger consumer appetite for discretionary spending due to lower housing costs.

title: Netflix becomes world's most valuable media company
summary: Netflix briefly became the world's most valuable media company, with its market value surpassing Disney's due to a significant surge in its stock price. This shift reflects the broader trend of consumers moving towards online streaming services, while traditional media companies like Disney are also adapting their strategies.

title: Netflix is now bigger than Disney by this one measure
summary: Netflix has surpassed Walt Disney Co. to become the leading U.S. media company by market value. This shift occurred after Netflix's market capitalization reached $153 billion on Thursday, exceeding Disney's $152 billion. Netflix had previously overtaken Comcast Corp. for the No. 2 position.

title: Kraft Heinz establishes Netherlands as ‘global growth engine’
summary: The Kraft Heinz Company has invested €90m over two years to establish the Netherlands as a "global growth engine," including opening a global center of excellence in Amsterdam. This center will focus on efficiency and innovation, leveraging local talent and deep historical ties, as the company aims to accelerate growth in the EMEA region. Additionally, Kraft Heinz is opening a new Heinz Ketchup line at its Elst production facility next year.

title: Icahn sells some of his Herbalife shares, remains biggest investor
summary: Billionaire investor Carl Icahn announced he has sold 11.4 million shares of Herbalife Nutrition Ltd, reducing his exposure to the nutrition company. Despite the sale, Icahn remains Herbalife's largest shareholder with five directors on its board and believes the company's future is bright. This move follows speculation about his stake and prominent short-seller William Ackman's exit from his bet against Herbalife.

title: El Banco Supervielle compró InvertirOnline
summary: Grupo Supervielle S.A. acquired 100% of the social capital of InvertirOnline ("IOL"), a leading financial market company and specialized online trading site in Argentina, for US$38.5 million. This acquisition allows Supervielle to enhance its digital transformation strategy and offer a more complete value proposition to its customers. IOL, founded in 1999, has approximately 16,400 users and AR$6.4 billion in assets under management, holding a significant share of the Argentine stock trading market.

The piece also discusses analyst opinions on Netflix's future amid increasing competition and advises on general investing strategies.

title: Halliburton and Saudi Aramco Reach Deal to Increase Gas Output
summary: Halliburton and Saudi Aramco have signed a three-year contract to increase gas production in three Saudi Arabian shale fields, signaling the expansion of the American shale gas revolution to the Middle East. This deal aims to support Saudi Aramco's growing chemical industry and reduce domestic oil consumption for power, thereby increasing crude exports. Halliburton, with its extensive experience in shale drilling globally, will provide technology, logistics management, and operational excellence to maximize Saudi Arabia's asset value.

title: Chubb Ltd: Collect Rising Dividends From This Overlooked Company
summary: Chubb Ltd (NYSE:CB) is highlighted as an overlooked company with a long history of consistently increasing its dividend. The article suggests that despite not frequently making headlines, the company has successfully raised its dividend every year for 25 years.

title: Mexico violence hits Canadian silver miner’s operations
summary: Pan American Silver Corp (PAAS.TO) has curtailed operations at its Dolores silver-gold mine in Chihuahua, Mexico, due to rising violence and security incidents affecting transport routes. This decision follows similar actions by other companies in Mexico facing increased gang violence and organized crime, leading to record murder rates and rampant freight thefts. Pan American Silver's shares were down over 5% following the announcement.

title: Halliburton rolls in stimulation crew at Strike’s trail blazing well
summary: Strike Energy is advancing its "Jaws-1" gas well project in South Australia, mobilizing Halliburton for a hydraulic stimulation program. This follows successful drilling and de-risking, with the project targeting significant coal seam gas reserves even at challenging depths. If successful, it could supply Australia's east coast domestic gas demand for up to 20 years.

title: Target plans three Seattle-area stores in urban, small-format push
summary: Target is planning to open three new small-format stores in the Seattle area as part of its strategy to expand into urban locations, dense suburban neighborhoods, and college campuses where traditional-sized Target stores are not feasible. These smaller stores aim to cater to areas with limited space and high population density. The company is pursuing this strategy to adapt to evolving retail landscapes and reach more customers in metropolitan environments.

title: AIG’s Duperreault introduces fund to boost Bermuda
summary: AIG CEO Brian Duperreault, alongside New Venture Holdings CEO Don Mackenzie and Arch Capital Group chief investment officer Preston Hutchings, has launched the Bermuda Infrastructure Fund. This fund, supported by several re/insurance companies, aims to invest in Bermuda's infrastructure projects. The initiative follows earlier efforts by Duperreault to bring private sector financial impetus to address the island's aging infrastructure and support new industries like insurtech.

title: Our Model Forecasts May Non-Farm Payroll, and June’s Too
summary: This article discusses a CME Group model that forecasts Non-Farm Payroll (NFP) results for May and June using three key factors: credit spreads, the shape of the yield curve, and changes in oil prices. The model explains approximately 70% of NFP variance, highlighting credit spreads as the most significant indicator. While forecasting continued job growth in the short term, the article warns of increasing risks of job losses in the early 2020s due to a flattening yield curve and potential credit spread widening.

title: $210M settlement eyed in Wilmington Trust shareholder suit
summary: Wilmington Trust has agreed to a $210 million settlement in a shareholder lawsuit, following the criminal conviction of four executives and $60 million in federal fines related to a scheme to conceal toxic commercial real-estate loans. If approved, the settlement, involving $200 million from M&T Bank and $10 million from KPMG, could compensate shareholders who bought stock between October 2009 and November 2010. This development comes shortly after the executives' convictions for bank fraud, conspiracy, and lying to regulators.

title: From Broke To Billionaire: How Fred Luddy Built The World’s Most Innovative Company
summary: This article chronicles the inspiring journey of Fred Luddy, who rose from financial hardship to found ServiceNow, a company recognized for its innovation. It details his entrepreneurial spirit and ability to build successful ventures despite personal setbacks, ultimately creating a billionaire-dollar enterprise.

title: Sonoco to close paperboard mill in Montreal
summary: Sonoco announced the permanent closure of its Montreal, Quebec, Canada, uncoated recycled paperboard mill, effective August 27, 2008. This decision, impacting 53 employees, is due to a significant downturn in the Canadian paper industry, declining demand for cores and coreboard, and escalating operational costs making the mill unprofitable at less than full capacity. Sonoco will continue to operate 23 paper mills globally and maintain operations at its Trent Valley and Brantford mills in Ontario to meet customer needs.

title: Senator Hassan Visits Timken Aerospace, Highlights Importance of Supporting Innovative Businesses in New Hampshire
summary: Senator Maggie Hassan visited Timken Aerospace in Lebanon, New Hampshire, to highlight the importance of supporting innovative businesses that contribute to job creation and economic development. During her visit, she toured the facility, met with employees, and discussed her efforts to ensure businesses like Timken have the necessary workforce and support to thrive. Timken Aerospace, a world-leading manufacturer of bearings and mechanical power transmission products, expressed gratitude for Senator Hassan's commitment to strengthening workforce development in the state.

title: Weyerhaeuser closing 340-employee plant in Arkansas
summary: Weyerhaeuser Company announced the immediate closure of its veneer and plywood facility in Mountain Pine, Arkansas, leading to the elimination of approximately 340 jobs. This decision is part of an ongoing strategic review to enhance shareholder value and reflects industry-wide market challenges for wood products. Weyerhaeuser will work with state and local leaders to assist with the transition while continuing to operate other businesses in Arkansas.

title: Dow drops nearly 400 points after Morgan Stanley, JP Morgan lead bank stock tumble
summary: U.S. stocks, led by bank shares, tumbled due to political turmoil in Italy and ongoing trade disputes with China. The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell almost 400 points, with major banks like Goldman Sachs and J.P. Morgan experiencing significant losses. The euro also dropped to its lowest level against the dollar this year amidst rising Italian debt rates and broader European market declines.

title: Garbage collectors in training bag good jobs
summary: A program called Civicorps in the East Bay is providing young adults, many from disadvantaged backgrounds, with high school diplomas and job training, leading to well-paying, unionized positions as garbage truck drivers for Waste Management of Alameda County Inc. The initiative offers a pathway to a secure career and benefits, with apprentices earning up to $56,000 annually and full-time drivers potentially making $80,000 per year plus overtime. Success stories like Khris Bland and Kiara Alexis highlight how the program transforms lives, offering financial stability and future prospects to participants.

title: KKR to buy BMC Software, 5 years after going private in a $6.9 billion deal
summary: KKR & Co. LP announced a deal to acquire BMC Software from an investor group led by Bain Capital Private Equity and Golden Gate Capital. This acquisition comes five years after BMC Software was taken private in a $6.9 billion deal. KKR anticipates the deal will close in the third quarter of 2018, with financing provided by several major banks.

summary: Palo Alto Networks (PANW) stock has broken out to an all-time high due to increased demand for cybersecurity solutions amidst a surge in cyber-attacks. The stock's healthy buying pressure since April 2017 has led to this bullish action, even as other tech stocks experienced a decline. However, a rising wedge pattern suggests potential vulnerability, and investors are advised to wait for the stock to exit this pattern before making new moves.

summary: Allegro Merger, a blank check company founded by Crescendo Partners' Eric Rosenfeld, filed for a $130 million IPO. The company plans to offer 13 million units at $10 each, valuing it at $166 million. Each unit comprises common stock, a warrant, and a right to receive a fraction of a share.

title: Gogo Welcomes Will Davis as Vice President of Investor Relations
summary: Gogo has appointed Will Davis as its new Vice President of Investor Relations. Davis brings nearly 20 years of experience in the wireless and communications industry, notably from Lumos Networks. His expertise is expected to be instrumental in driving value for Gogo and its shareholders.

title: Entergy, NextEra Energy Resources celebrate commissioning of Arkansas' largest universal solar energy project
summary: Entergy Arkansas and NextEra Energy Resources celebrated the commissioning of the Stuttgart Solar Energy Center, Arkansas' largest universal solar project. This 81-megawatt facility, located near Stuttgart, Ark., is expected to power over 13,000 homes and generate nearly $8 million in tax revenue for Arkansas County, benefiting local schools. The project marks a significant step in diversifying Arkansas's energy portfolio with clean, renewable solar power.

title: Microsoft is now more valuable than Alphabet — by about $10 billion
summary: Microsoft has surpassed Alphabet in market capitalization, becoming the world's third most valuable company. This shift occurred as Microsoft's market value reached $749 billion compared to Alphabet's $739 billion, largely driven by significant growth in Microsoft's cloud computing business. Microsoft's stock surged 40 percent over the past 12 months, greatly outpacing Alphabet's gains.

title: Old Dominion Opens $10 Million Facility in Central Florida
summary: Old Dominion Freight Line Inc. has opened a new $10 million service center in North Lakeland, Fla., to accommodate growth in central Florida and relieve pressure on its Tampa center. The company, which is based in Thomasville, N.C., expects to create more jobs as the facility expands, which currently employs 33 people transferring from other centers. This new facility is Old Dominion's 11th in Florida and is strategically located to serve major customers like Publix Super Markets Inc., with whom Old Dominion conducts $10 million in business.

title: How Leidos basks in the halo effect of the Capitals' Stanley Cup run
summary: Reston government contractor Leidos Holdings is benefiting from increased brand exposure due to the Washington Capitals' Stanley Cup run. Leidos, a legacy sponsor of Monumental Sports & Entertainment since 2014, is gaining significant off-ice "bounce" from the team's participation in the finals. This sponsorship includes events like the Hockey Fights Cancer night, further elevating the company's profile during this high-profile sports event.

title: Important update: EOS token swap and trading halt
summary: eToro announced an important update regarding the EOS token swap from Ethereum to its new MainNet chain. The platform will manage the transition for clients, but EOS trading will be halted for an undetermined period due to expected low liquidity around June 2nd, 2018. Clients can keep positions open to participate in the swap or close them beforehand, but will not be able to adjust open EOS positions during the halt.

title: Exelon Cuts Jobs Ahead of Oyster Creek Closure
summary: Exelon Corporation is initiating job cuts at its Oyster Creek Nuclear Generating Station in New Jersey ahead of its scheduled closure in October. Approximately 84 employees will be the first to leave, with the company pledging to offer positions elsewhere within Exelon to employees who wish to stay. The closure is part of a deal with state regulators and comes amid historically low power prices impacting nuclear and coal plants.

Pan American projects significant silver and gold production for the full year 2018 and from its Argentine mines through 2021.

summary: Microchip Technology Inc. (MCHP) has completed its acquisition of Microsemi Corporation for $10.3 billion, a deal announced on March 1, 2018. title: For Now It’s Best to Avoid Colgate-Palmolive Company Stock
summary: Despite recent improvements in revenue and earnings, and a long tradition of dividend increases, Colgate-Palmolive (CL) stock is seen as a cautious investment due to its no-moat status. The rise of e-commerce has intensified competition for highly commoditized products, making it harder for large consumer goods companies to maintain their market dominance. While Colgate-Palmolive retains a loyal customer base and stability, the author suggests its current valuation at 20 times earnings is too high given the increased competitive threats.

summary: Paul Jones, a Harrisburg High School graduate, achieved significant success in industrial business through hard work and education, holding top positions at companies like A.O. Smith Corp. and Rexnord Corp. He attributes his success to early jobs and his parents' encouragement to give back, leading him to support his former high school. Jones emphasizes that his family is his proudest achievement.

title: Assurant adding 300 jobs to bulk up tech center in Gwinnett
summary: Assurant, a $6 billion-a-year insurance company, is adding 300 jobs to expand its technology arm in Gwinnett County, Georgia. This expansion involves a new tech support center in Duluth, catering to the growing demand for device insurance and support for smart devices. The company plans to recruit primarily from the local Gwinnett County and metro Atlanta talent pool for positions including technical support analysts, supervisors, and trainers.

title: Dollar-Store Chains Dented by Cool Weather, Rising Costs
summary: Dollar General and Dollar Tree reported weaker-than-expected sales growth due to cool spring weather and increased freight and wage costs, leading to a decline in their stock prices. Dollar General's same-store sales rose 2.1%, missing analyst estimates of 3%, while Dollar Tree's same-store sales grew 1.4%, falling short of 2.3% estimates.

title: Tariff winners and losers: How Trump's trade spat could affect shoppers
summary: President Trump's imposition of tariffs on imported steel and aluminum is expected to impact consumer prices and company profits, leading to both winners and losers in various industries. American steel and aluminum producers are poised to benefit, while industries like whiskey, motorcycles, and drinks using aluminum cans face potential cost increases and retaliatory tariffs from other countries. The market reacted negatively, with the Dow Jones industrial average falling, as investors fear a trade war could crimp profits of companies and raise consumer prices.

title: Halliburton CEO Says Oil at $70 Is "Good Enough"
summary: Halliburton CEO Jeff Miller is unconcerned by plunging oil prices, stating that oil trading around $70 a barrel keeps the industry healthy. Despite OPEC's talks of increased production and global unrest, Miller believes supply and demand are back in balance, providing comfort in the $60-$70 range. Halliburton, a major oil field service company, saw revenues surge 30% to $20 billion in 2017 due to strong drilling demand in North America and is now hiring again after a deep downturn that led to significant layoffs.

title: Modine to cut staff by 25% at its HQ in Wisconsin
summary: Modine Manufacturing Company announced a 25% workforce reduction at its Racine, Wis., headquarters, impacting approximately 170 employees and contractors. This action is part of a restructuring program to reduce costs and restore profitability to its global operations, which have been severely affected by the worldwide economic crisis. Modine also plans significant workforce reductions at its European headquarters in Germany and will discuss further restructuring activities when it announces its Q3 fiscal 2009 results.

title: Fortune 500 Company Mosaic To Relocate Corporate Headquarters To Hillsborough
summary: The Mosaic Company (NYSE: MOS), a Fortune 500 firm and global leader in potash and phosphates, announced its intention to move its corporate headquarters from Minnesota to Hillsborough County, Florida. This strategic relocation aims to enhance efficiency, achieve cost savings, and strengthen connections with its significantly expanded South American operations and local Florida communities. The move is expected to benefit Mosaic by improving access to its Mosaic Fertilizantes business in Brazil and deepening its engagement within Central Florida where it already has a major presence.

title: Sneak Peek: Massive Norwegian Bliss sails into Seattle for Alaska cruise season (Photos)
summary: The Norwegian Bliss cruise ship, the newest vessel from Norwegian Cruise Line Holdings Inc., has arrived in Seattle for the Alaska cruise season. This 20-story ship, capable of carrying 4,004 people, is expected to bring significant economic benefits to Pacific Northwest suppliers. Port of Seattle officials anticipate the ship will boost demand for local food, fresh produce, and wines.

title: PepsiCo rated among top global companies for leaders
summary: PepsiCo Inc. has been named to the 2009 list of Global Top Companies for Leaders, a comprehensive study conducted by Hewitt Associates, The RBL Group, and Fortune. This recognition highlights PepsiCo's commitment to "Performance with Purpose" and talent sustainability, even through economic downturns. The study found that Global Top Companies prioritize building leadership capability and intensely focus on talent development, aligning leadership programs with business goals.

title: Rio Tinto Alcan to restart idled capacity at Quebec refinery
summary: Rio Tinto Alcan is restarting idled production capacity at its Vaudreuil alumina refinery in Quebec due to current market conditions, after curtailing 25% of its production last January. This move will not affect the permanent workforce and some contractors are expected to be recalled. The Vaudreuil plant's ability to operate at variable production levels is crucial for its sustained competitiveness and viability.

summary: The municipal bond market has outperformed Treasuries and corporates year-to-date, with municipal High Yield being a top performer. title: ConocoPhillips fined $180K for 2016 pipeline leak in northwest Alberta
summary: ConocoPhillips Canada has been fined $180,000 for a 2016 pipeline leak that spilled 380,000 litres of condensate in northwestern Alberta, leading to the deaths of at least 38 wildlife species and affecting nearly three square kilometres of land. The Alberta Energy Regulator cited the company for failing to detect the leak when it began, not reporting it immediately for 33 days, and for failing to maintain a leak-detection manual and take reasonable remedial measures. This delay in reporting and action reportedly worsened environmental damage, including the loss of fish spawning output in Webb Creek for a year.

title: Blackstone, Solus settle Hovnanian credit default swap dispute

title: Goldman Sachs junior banker charged in Insider Trading scheme

title: U.S. Supreme Court Overturns Quill's Physical Presence Rule
summary: The U.S. Supreme Court, in South Dakota v. Wayfair Inc., overturned the long-standing physical presence rule established in Quill Corp. v. North Dakota and National Bellas Hess, Inc. v. Department of Revenue of Ill. This decision allows states to require out-of-state retailers, particularly online sellers, to collect and remit sales taxes even if they do not have a physical presence in the state, provided they meet certain economic nexus thresholds. The Court cited the outdated nature of the physical presence rule in the age of e-commerce and its creation of market distortions and significant revenue losses for states as primary reasons for its decision.
